steps.title: Confirm the opportunity record exists in the PPM tool
sop: Open the pipeline register in the PPM tool and locate the opportunity by ID.
Confirm the stage, LOB, and segment fields are populated.
Note any existing owner value that will need closing off.
Done when the opportunity record is confirmed and its current owner state noted.
verify: Read the opportunity record fields on screen.
Pass when the record exists with a populated stage and LOB.

steps.title: Select a candidate owner with available capacity
sop: Review candidate product owners against their current opportunity load.
Check the PPM resource view for capacity in the opportunity stage window.
Shortlist a candidate whose capacity covers the expected effort.
Done when a candidate with available capacity is selected.
verify: Check the candidate allocation in the PPM resource view.
Pass when the candidate has capacity for the opportunity stage window.

steps.title: Run a conflict of interest check on the candidate
sop: Check the candidate declarations register for interests in the target segment or partner.
Ask the candidate to confirm no undeclared conflict exists.
Record the check result against the opportunity record.
Done when the conflict check result is recorded for the candidate.
verify: Read the recorded conflict check result on the opportunity record.
Pass when a clear check result is recorded before assignment.

steps.title: Obtain written acceptance from the candidate owner
sop: Send the candidate the opportunity scope, expected effort, and accountabilities.
Request written acceptance or a decline with reason.
Save the acceptance correspondence to the opportunity folder in SharePoint.
Done when written acceptance or decline is received and filed.
verify: Retrieve the acceptance correspondence from the opportunity folder.
Pass when a written acceptance exists for the assigned owner.

steps.title: Name a deputy for continuity
sop: Agree a deputy with the accepted owner for absence cover.
Confirm the deputy accepts the standby accountability.
Record the deputy name on the opportunity record.
Done when a named and accepting deputy is recorded.
verify: Read the deputy field on the opportunity record.
Pass when a named deputy with recorded acceptance is present.

steps.title: Record the assignment and close the prior owner field
sop: Populate the owner field with the accepted owner name and set the assignment date.
Close off any prior owner value with an end date so history is preserved.
Confirm the opportunity remains in an active stage after the update.
Done when the owner, assignment date, and prior owner closure are recorded.
verify: Run the register report filtered to active opportunities without an owner.
Pass when the report returns no rows for this opportunity.

generic.Defined scope/population: Unmet customer needs relevant to the opportunity drawn from interviews, surveys, complaints, and broker feedback.
generic.In-scope period: The feedback and complaint window agreed for mining, with the extract dates recorded per source.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each need row carries the outcome statement, evidence source, observation count, and customer segment.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Need evidence counts reconcile to the CRM and complaint extract record counts for the period.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Needs workbook versioned in SharePoint with the CRM extract date recorded on the source tab.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Needs with only a single weak evidence source logged as unvalidated pending further research.
generic.Test population: Every unmet need row captured in the needs documentation for the opportunity.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any need is phrased as a product feature or the shared document retains a customer identifier.
generic.Exception handling path: Feature-phrased needs are rewritten as outcomes and identifier breaches are redacted immediately.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Needs are accepted when each is an outcome statement with a cited source, count, and segment.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint opportunity needs workbook plus the CRM extract used as the feedback source.

steps.title: Extract customer feedback themes from the CRM
sop: Query the CRM for feedback, complaint, and service interaction records for the target segment.
Limit the extract to the agreed feedback window and record the extract date.
Load the extract into Excel as the raw evidence tab.
Done when the CRM feedback extract is loaded with its extract date.
verify: Compare the extract record count against the CRM query result count.
Pass when the loaded count matches the CRM query count.

steps.title: Mine complaint and service data for recurring themes
sop: Group the extracted records by root cause and presenting issue.
Count occurrences per theme so frequency is measurable.
Retain only themes relevant to the opportunity scope.
Done when recurring themes are identified with occurrence counts.
verify: Sum theme counts against the filtered extract record count.
Pass when the theme counts reconcile to the source extract.

steps.title: Write each unmet need as a customer outcome
sop: Convert each theme into a statement of the outcome the customer cannot achieve.
Avoid naming any product, feature, or solution in the need statement.
Rewrite any statement that reads as a feature request.
Done when every need is expressed as a customer outcome.
verify: Read each need statement for product or feature language.
Pass when no need statement names a product feature or solution.

steps.title: Cite the evidence source and count for each need
sop: Record the source type for each need such as interview, survey, complaint, or broker feedback.
Record the number of observations supporting the need.
Mark needs supported by a single weak source as unvalidated.
Done when every need carries a source type and an observation count.
verify: Filter the needs list for blank source or count cells.
Pass when no need row is missing its source type or count.

steps.title: Segment each need by the customer segment observed
sop: Assign each need the customer segment it was observed in from the taxonomy.
Split needs observed differently across segments into separate rows.
Confirm the segments used match the opportunity target market definition.
Done when every need is assigned to an observed customer segment.
verify: Filter the needs list for blank segment values.
Pass when every need row carries a segment from the taxonomy.

steps.title: Remove customer identifiers from the shared needs document
sop: Search the needs workbook for customer names, policy numbers, and contact details.
Mask or remove identifiers so the shared document holds no direct identifier.
Keep the linkage key in a restricted file only if traceability is required.
Done when the shared needs document is free of direct identifiers.
verify: Run an identifier pattern search across the shared workbook.
Pass when no customer name or policy number is found.

steps.title: Link the needs documentation to the opportunity record
sop: Version the needs workbook and save it to the SharePoint opportunity folder.
Link the workbook to the opportunity record so it is discoverable.
Notify the opportunity owner that the needs set is available.
Done when the needs workbook is filed and linked to the opportunity.
verify: Open the opportunity record and follow the needs workbook link.
Pass when the link resolves to the current versioned needs workbook.

generic.Defined scope/population: The market, geography, and time period defined for the opportunity market scan.
generic.In-scope period: The scan period stated in the findings document with source retrieval dates recorded.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each statistic carries a value, a named source, a retrieval date, and the period it covers.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Internal market figures reconcile to the warehouse extract used, with the extract date recorded.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Scan findings document versioned in SharePoint under the opportunity ID with source citations.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Statistics that could not be sourced logged as gaps with the impact on conclusions noted.
generic.Test population: Every market statistic and finding in the scan findings document.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any market statistic has no cited source and retrieval date.
generic.Exception handling path: Unsourced statistics are removed or downgraded to an assumption before findings are issued.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The scan is accepted when findings are stated as implications for the opportunity, not raw data alone.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint opportunity folder scan findings document plus the BI report of internal market data.

steps.title: Define the market, geography, and period for the scan
sop: State the market, geography, and time period the scan will cover.
Agree the scope with the Insurance Product Manager before research starts.
Record the scope statement at the head of the findings document.
Done when the scan scope is stated and agreed.
verify: Read the scope statement against the opportunity target market.
Pass when market, geography, and period are all explicitly stated.

steps.title: Collect market size, growth, and loss trend figures
sop: Gather market size, growth rate, and loss trend from external and internal sources.
Record the source name and retrieval date against each figure.
Pull internal comparators from the warehouse and record the extract date.
Done when each headline figure is recorded with its source and date.
verify: Filter the figures table for blank source or retrieval date cells.
Pass when no figure is recorded without a source and date.

steps.title: Capture emerging risk and regulatory-change signals
sop: Scan regulatory publications and industry commentary for changes affecting the market.
Record each signal with its source, date, and expected effect on the market.
Exclude signals with no credible source rather than reporting them as findings.
Done when relevant emerging risk and regulatory signals are captured with sources.
verify: Check each captured signal cites a named publication and date.
Pass when no signal is recorded without a credible cited source.

steps.title: Describe distribution channel structure and share
sop: Identify the channels through which the market is served and their relative share.
Source channel share figures and record the source and date.
Note channel concentration or lock-in that would affect market entry.
Done when channel structure and share are described with sources.
verify: Check the channel share figures sum consistently and cite sources.

steps.title: Cross-check internal figures against the BI platform
sop: Compare internal market figures in the scan against the BI platform reports.

Record the comparison result in the findings document.
Done when internal figures reconcile to the BI platform reports.

Pass when internal figures agree with the BI reports within tolerance.

steps.title: Translate findings into implications for the opportunity
sop: Write an implications section stating what each finding means for our opportunity.
State clearly where a finding supports or challenges the opportunity hypothesis.

Done when every material finding carries a stated implication.
verify: Read the findings against the implications section for coverage.
Pass when no material finding is left without an implication.

steps.title: Version and file the scan findings under the opportunity ID
sop: Version the findings document and stamp it with the scan completion date.
Save it to the SharePoint opportunity folder using the opportunity ID naming convention.
Notify the opportunity owner that the scan findings are available.
Done when the versioned findings are filed under the opportunity ID.

Pass when the versioned scan findings document is returned.

generic.Defined scope/population: The product concept brief covering the problem statement, opportunity hypothesis, and target market for the opportunity.

generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The brief is accepted when it contains problem statement, hypothesis, and target market sections in full.

steps.title: Gather the research artifacts to cite in the brief

Record each artifact name, version, and location for citation.
Confirm each artifact is the current version before citing it.
Done when the citation list is complete with versions.
verify: Open each cited artifact from its recorded location.
Pass when every cited artifact resolves at the recorded version.

steps.title: Write the problem statement naming the affected segment

Name the customer segment that experiences the problem.
Quantify the impact on that segment using the needs evidence.
Done when the problem statement names the segment and its impact.
verify: Read the problem statement for segment and impact.
Pass when it is framed as a customer problem with a named segment.

steps.title: Write the opportunity hypothesis in testable form
sop: State the proposed intervention and the expected measurable outcome.
State the condition or observation that would disprove the hypothesis.

Done when the hypothesis states both the expected outcome and the disproof condition.
verify: Read the hypothesis for an explicit disproof condition.
Pass when a falsifying condition is stated.

steps.title: Define the target market and the customers out of scope
sop: State the intended target market using the segment taxonomy.
State explicitly which customers the product is not intended for.
Align both statements with the segments in the needs evidence.
Done when both the target market and out-of-scope customers are stated.
verify: Read the target market section for both statements.
Pass when the brief names both who the product is for and who it is not for.

steps.title: Separate assumptions from evidenced facts
sop: Review every claim in the brief for a supporting cited artifact.
Move unsupported claims into a clearly labelled assumptions section.
Assign a validation owner to each assumption.
Done when unsupported claims sit in the assumptions section with owners.
verify: Scan the brief body for claims without a citation.
Pass when no unsourced claim remains in the factual sections.

steps.title: Publish the drafted brief to SharePoint and Confluence
sop: Version the brief and save it to the SharePoint opportunity folder.
Create the Confluence opportunity page linking to the SharePoint brief.
Set the brief status to draft pending stakeholder validation.
Done when the versioned draft brief is published in both locations.
verify: Open the Confluence page and follow the brief link.
Pass when the link resolves to the current versioned draft brief.

generic.Defined scope/population: The handover pack and stage transition from opportunity definition to the Coverage & Product Design team.

steps.title: Assemble the handover pack in SharePoint

Place them in a single handover folder under the opportunity ID.
List the contents on a handover checklist with each item version.
Done when the handover folder holds every checklist item.

steps.title: List open questions with owners for the design stage

Assign each an owner who carries it into the design stage.

Done when every open question carries an owner and a resolution point.
verify: Filter the open question list for blank owners.

steps.title: Grant the design team access to the opportunity folder
sop: Add the Coverage & Product Design group to the opportunity folder permissions.
Confirm access covers the handover pack and the research artifacts.
Remove any inherited restriction blocking the design group.
Done when the design team holds read access to the opportunity folder.
verify: Ask a design team member to open the handover folder.
Pass when the design team member can retrieve the pack.

steps.title: Walk the design lead through the pack
sop: Hold a handover session covering brief, constraints, sizing, and open questions.
Answer design team questions and note any that need follow-up.
Add newly raised questions to the open question list with owners.
Done when the handover session is held and questions are captured.
verify: Compare the session notes against the open question list.
Pass when every question raised in session appears on the list with an owner.

steps.title: Record the design lead acceptance of the handover
sop: Confirm no handover checklist item remains outstanding.
Record the Coverage & Product Design lead acceptance with name and date.
File the acceptance record in the handover folder.
Done when acceptance is recorded with no outstanding checklist item.
verify: Read the checklist status at the acceptance timestamp.
Pass when no item is marked outstanding when acceptance was recorded.

steps.title: Advance the pipeline register stage to design
sop: Open the opportunity in the PPM tool and set the stage to design.
Record the stage transition date and the acceptance reference.
Confirm the stage history retains the prior stage entry.
Done when the register shows the design stage with a transition date.
verify: Open the PPM stage history for the opportunity.
Pass when the design stage transition is recorded with its acceptance date.

generic.Defined scope/population: The problem statement and opportunity hypothesis framed from the captured unmet customer needs.

generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Alternative framings considered and rejected recorded with the rationale for rejection.

steps.title: Load the captured needs into the framing workbook

Copy the need identifiers, statements, and segments into the framing workbook.
Retain the need identifiers so the framing can reference them.

State the measurable outcome expected if the intervention works.
State the observation that would show the hypothesis is wrong.

Pass when a falsifying observation is explicitly stated.

steps.title: Write the validation success criteria before design begins
sop: Define the evidence and thresholds that would validate the hypothesis.
State the research method that will produce that evidence.

verify: Compare the criteria date against the design stage start date.
Pass when the criteria predate the start of design.

steps.title: Record alternative framings considered and rejected
sop: List the alternative problem framings the team considered.

Done when every rejected framing is recorded with its rationale.
verify: Read the rejected framings section for rationale coverage.

steps.title: Version and file the framing document
sop: Version the framing document and cite the needs workbook version used.
Save it to the SharePoint opportunity folder.
Circulate it to the concept brief author as the drafting input.

verify: Open the filed document and check the needs workbook citation.
Pass when the cited needs version matches the workbook used.

generic.Defined scope/population: The Pricing & Product Committee pre-approval decision on proceeding from opportunity to formal design.
generic.In-scope period: The committee cycle in which the concept brief is tabled for the pre-approval decision.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Minute records decision, quorum, recusals, conditions with owners, and the concept brief version tabled.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Attendee count in the minute meets the committee quorum threshold in the terms of reference.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Committee pack and signed minute filed in SharePoint with the meeting date and brief version.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Conditions attached to the pre-approval logged with an owner and the gate they must be met by.
generic.Test population: The committee pack, the minute, and the pipeline register entry for the opportunity.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if the minute omits the decision, quorum, or the concept brief version referenced.
generic.Exception handling path: An incomplete minute is returned to the committee secretary for correction before the register is updated.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Pre-approval is accepted when a minuted decision references the concept brief version and is recorded on the register.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint committee folder holding the pack and minute plus the PPM tool opportunity record.

steps.title: Assemble the committee pack with the concept brief
sop: Attach the current concept brief version to the committee pack.
Include the market sizing, constraints, and appetite assessment summaries.
State the decision requested and the conditions the team proposes.
Done when the pack is assembled with the brief version stated.
verify: Open the pack and check the brief version citation.
Pass when the pack cites the current concept brief version.

steps.title: Circulate the pack ahead of the committee meeting
sop: Send the pack to committee members by the pre-read deadline.
Save the circulation record with its send timestamp.
Chase members who confirm they have not received it.
Done when the pack is circulated within the pre-read deadline.
verify: Compare the circulation timestamp against the pre-read deadline.
Pass when circulation precedes the deadline.

steps.title: Provide the actuarial view at the committee
sop: Present the actuarial view on loss predictability and data availability for the concept.
State any assumption the committee should treat as unvalidated.
Answer committee questions on actuarial viability.
Done when the actuarial view is presented and questions answered.
verify: Check the minute records the actuarial view and any caveats.
Pass when the actuarial position is captured in the minute.

steps.title: Confirm quorum and record recusals
sop: Check attendance against the committee terms of reference quorum requirement.
Record any member recused due to a conflict on this concept.
Defer the decision if quorum is not met.
Done when quorum is confirmed and recusals are recorded.
verify: Compare the attendee count against the quorum threshold.
Pass when quorum is met and recusals are recorded in the minute.

steps.title: Record the decision and its conditions in the minute
sop: Record the decision as proceed, proceed-with-conditions, or decline.
List each condition with a named owner and the stage gate it must be met by.
Reference the concept brief version the decision applies to.
Done when the minute records a clear decision with conditions and brief version.
verify: Read the minute for the decision wording and brief version.
Pass when a single clear decision references the brief version.

steps.title: Update the pipeline register with the decision
sop: Record the decision, decision date, and minute reference on the PPM opportunity record.
Load each condition as a tracked item with its owner and gate.
Advance or hold the opportunity stage according to the decision.
Done when the register reflects the decision, date, and minute reference.
verify: Open the PPM opportunity record and read the decision fields.
Pass when decision, date, and minute reference are all recorded.

generic.Defined scope/population: The premium pool and three-year revenue potential estimate for the opportunity target market.
generic.In-scope period: Year one through year three from the assumed launch date, with the warehouse extract as-at date recorded.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Exposure counts, average premium, penetration assumption, and low, base, and high cases are populated.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Model output for any existing comparable book reconciles to warehouse premium for the same period.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Model workbook versioned with an assumption tab naming source and owner per assumption.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Assumptions with no benchmark logged as unbenchmarked with the validation owner and date.
generic.Test population: Every assumption cell and every calculation cell in the premium pool model.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any calculation cell contains a hardcoded value with no assumption reference.
generic.Exception handling path: Hardcoded values are replaced with referenced assumptions or logged as exceptions before sign-off.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The estimate is accepted when a documented assumption tab names source and owner for every assumption.
generic.Evidence location: The Excel model workbook in SharePoint plus the warehouse extract and actuarial platform outputs.

steps.title: Extract exposure counts for the target market
sop: Query the warehouse for exposure or household counts in the target segment and geography.
Record the query text and the as-at date on the model source tab.
Load the counts into the model as a referenced input, not a typed constant.
Done when exposure counts are loaded with query and as-at date recorded.
verify: Trace the model exposure input back to the source tab.
Pass when the input references the extract rather than a typed value.

steps.title: Set average premium from comparable book data
sop: Derive average premium from a comparable in-force book or an actuarial indication.
Record the comparable used and the period it covers on the assumption tab.
Name the owner accountable for the average premium assumption.
Done when average premium is set with a source and named owner.
verify: Read the assumption tab row for average premium.
Pass when source, period, and owner are all recorded.

steps.title: Benchmark the penetration assumption against a comparable launch
sop: Identify a comparable product launch and its achieved penetration curve.
Set the penetration assumption against that benchmark rather than by judgement alone.
Record the benchmark launch, its period, and the adjustment rationale.
Done when the penetration assumption cites a comparable launch benchmark.
verify: Read the assumption tab penetration row for the benchmark citation.
Pass when a named comparable launch supports the penetration figure.

steps.title: Build the year one to year three revenue projection
sop: Project premium separately for year one, year two, and year three.
Show volume and average premium as separate drivers in each year.
Avoid presenting a single blended multi-year figure.
Done when revenue is projected separately for each of the three years.
verify: Inspect the projection tab for three distinct year columns.
Pass when each year shows volume and average premium separately.

steps.title: Reconcile the model to warehouse premium for the comparable book
sop: Run the model logic against the existing comparable book for a historic period.
Compare the modelled result against actual warehouse premium for that period.
Investigate and document any difference beyond the agreed tolerance.
Done when the model reconciles to warehouse premium within tolerance.
verify: Read the reconciliation tab difference figure.
Pass when the difference sits within the agreed tolerance or is explained.

steps.title: Produce a low, base, and high sensitivity range
sop: Flex the penetration and average premium assumptions to low and high cases.
Recalculate the premium pool for each case using the actuarial platform where required.
Record which assumption drives most of the range.
Done when low, base, and high premium pool figures are produced.
verify: Check the three cases derive from flexed assumption cells.
Pass when each case recalculates from the assumption tab, not manual entry.

steps.title: Complete the assumption tab and audit for hardcoded values
sop: List every assumption with its value, source, owner, and last review date.
Trace every calculation cell to an assumption tab reference.
Replace any hardcoded constant with a referenced assumption.
Done when no calculation cell holds an unreferenced constant.
verify: Run a formula audit for constants inside calculation cells.
Pass when no calculation cell contains a hardcoded value without a reference.

generic.Defined scope/population: The new opportunity intake entry created in the product pipeline register in the PPM tool.
generic.In-scope period: The intake window from the opportunity being raised to the register entry being created and timestamped.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Opportunity ID, originator, LOB, segment, date raised, stage, and brief location are all populated.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: The new opportunity ID is unique across the register with no duplicate open entry for the same LOB and segment.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Register entry retained with creation timestamp and the stage change history in the PPM tool.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Potential duplicates found during the search logged with the decision to merge or proceed separately.
generic.Test population: The new register entry and the existing open opportunities for the same LOB and segment.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any mandatory intake field is blank or a duplicate open opportunity exists for the same LOB and segment.
generic.Exception handling path: Duplicates are merged with the originating entry and the merge recorded before the intake completes.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Intake is accepted when a unique ID with complete mandatory fields is created and timestamped.
generic.Evidence location: PPM tool pipeline register entry plus the SharePoint opportunity folder holding the concept brief.

steps.title: Search the register for duplicate or overlapping opportunities
sop: Search the pipeline register by LOB, segment, and keyword before creating the entry.
Review any open opportunity that overlaps in scope.
Log potential duplicates with the decision to merge or proceed separately.
Done when the duplicate search is complete and logged.
verify: Re-run the duplicate search after logging.
Pass when no unmerged duplicate open opportunity remains for the LOB and segment.

steps.title: Generate the unique opportunity ID
sop: Create the register entry so the PPM tool generates a unique opportunity ID.
Record the generated ID for use across all downstream artifacts.
Confirm the ID does not collide with an archived opportunity ID.
Done when a unique opportunity ID is generated and recorded.
verify: Search the register for the generated ID.
Pass when exactly one record is returned for the ID.

steps.title: Populate the mandatory intake fields
sop: Enter originator, line of business, customer segment, and date raised.
Set the opportunity stage to intake.
Complete any additional mandatory field the register requires.
Done when every mandatory intake field is populated.
verify: Run the register completeness report for the new entry.
Pass when no mandatory field is blank.

steps.title: Create the opportunity folder and link the concept brief
sop: Create the SharePoint opportunity folder named with the opportunity ID.
Place the concept brief in the folder if one already exists.
Record the folder link on the register entry.
Done when the register entry links to the opportunity folder location.
verify: Follow the register link from a non-author account.
Pass when the link resolves to the opportunity folder.

steps.title: Timestamp the intake stage change
sop: Set the stage to intake and save so the stage change is timestamped.
Confirm the stage history shows the intake entry with its timestamp.
Correct the stage if it defaulted to another value.
Done when the intake stage change is timestamped in the history.
verify: Open the stage history for the opportunity.
Pass when the intake stage change carries a timestamp.

steps.title: Review the completed intake entry
sop: Review the entry for field accuracy against the originator submission.
Confirm the duplicate search log is attached to the entry.
Correct or return the entry where information is inaccurate.
Done when the reviewed entry is confirmed accurate.
verify: Compare the register fields against the originator submission.
Pass when the register values match the submission.

generic.Defined scope/population: Total addressable, serviceable, and obtainable market for the opportunity geography and segment scope.
generic.In-scope period: The vintage of the external datasets used and the warehouse extract date for internal inputs.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each sizing input carries a value, source name, dataset vintage, and the scope it applies to.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Top-down and bottom-up sizing results reconcile on the reconciliation tab with variance explained.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Sizing model versioned in SharePoint with source names, vintages, and the extract date recorded.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Inputs without a credible source logged as estimates with the validation owner and impact noted.
generic.Test population: Every sizing input and both sizing method outputs in the model workbook.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any external data input lacks a source name and vintage or TAM, SAM, and SOM are conflated.
generic.Exception handling path: Unsourced inputs are replaced or downgraded to estimates and excluded from the headline figure.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Sizing is accepted when the reconciliation tab compares both methods and sensitivities are shown.
generic.Evidence location: The Excel sizing model in SharePoint plus the BI report and warehouse extract behind internal inputs.

steps.title: Define the geographic and segment scope for the sizing
sop: Take the target market definition from the concept brief.
State the geography and segments the sizing will cover.
Confirm the scope matches the brief before building the model.
Done when the sizing scope is stated and matches the brief.
verify: Compare the sizing scope statement against the brief target market.
Pass when geography and segment scope match the brief.

steps.title: Build the top-down sizing from external datasets
sop: Source total market premium or exposure from a named external dataset.
Record the dataset name and its vintage on the source tab.
Narrow from total market to the serviceable scope using stated filters.
Done when the top-down estimate is built with sourced inputs.
verify: Filter the source tab for inputs with blank source or vintage.
Pass when every external input carries a source name and vintage.

steps.title: Build the bottom-up sizing from exposure counts
sop: Query the warehouse for exposure or household counts within scope.
Multiply counts by an evidenced average premium to build the estimate.
Record the extract date and the average premium source.
Done when the bottom-up estimate is built from counts and average premium.
verify: Trace the bottom-up result to the exposure extract and premium source.
Pass when both inputs are traceable and dated.

steps.title: Distinguish TAM, SAM, and SOM explicitly
sop: Present total addressable, serviceable, and obtainable market as separate figures.
State the filter that reduces each level to the next.
Avoid presenting a single market size number without qualification.
Done when all three levels are shown with their reduction filters.
verify: Read the output tab for three distinct labelled figures.
Pass when TAM, SAM, and SOM are separately stated with filters.

steps.title: Reconcile the top-down and bottom-up results
sop: Place both results side by side on a reconciliation tab.
Quantify the variance and identify the drivers of the difference.
Adjust or document the variance where it exceeds the agreed tolerance.
Done when the reconciliation tab shows both results and the variance.
verify: Open the reconciliation tab and read the variance figure.
Pass when both estimates are compared and the variance is explained.

steps.title: Show sensitivity to the two largest assumptions
sop: Identify the two assumptions with the greatest effect on the result.
Flex each to a low and high value and record the resulting sizing range.
Present the sensitivity alongside the headline figure.
Done when the sensitivity of the two largest assumptions is shown.
verify: Check the sensitivity output recalculates from the assumption cells.
Pass when the range derives from flexed assumptions, not manual entry.

steps.title: Review the model and publish it to the opportunity folder
sop: Review scope, sourcing, and reconciliation before publication.
Challenge any unsourced input and require correction.
Version the model and save it to the opportunity folder.
Done when the reviewed model is versioned and published.
verify: Open the published model and inspect the source tab.
Pass when no external input is missing a source name and vintage.

generic.Defined scope/population: The concept brief circulated to underwriting, actuarial, and distribution stakeholders for validation.
generic.In-scope period: The validation window from brief circulation to reissue of the revised version with changes highlighted.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each feedback item carries reviewer, function, comment, disposition, and rationale.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Feedback log item count equals the total comments received across the three functions.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Written feedback and the revised brief version retained in the SharePoint opportunity folder.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Rejected or deferred feedback logged with the rationale and the person who decided.
generic.Test population: Every feedback item received from underwriting, actuarial, and distribution reviewers.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any feedback item is left without a disposition or a function returned no written feedback.
generic.Exception handling path: Missing function feedback is chased and escalated to the function lead before the brief is reissued.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Validation is accepted when a revised brief version is reissued with all feedback dispositioned.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint opportunity folder feedback log, reviewer correspondence, and revised brief version.

steps.title: Circulate the concept brief to the three review functions
sop: Send the current brief version to named underwriting, actuarial, and distribution reviewers.
State the specific questions each function is asked to address.
Set a return date and the format for written feedback.
Done when all three functions hold the brief with a return date.
verify: Check the circulation record names a reviewer in each function.
Pass when all three functions have a named reviewer and a return date.

steps.title: Obtain the actuarial view on loss assumption plausibility
sop: Review the loss assumptions implied by the concept against available data.
State whether the assumptions are plausible and what data would confirm them.
Return the view in writing referencing the brief version.
Done when a written actuarial view on loss assumptions is returned.
verify: Read the actuarial response for an explicit loss assumption comment.
Pass when the response addresses loss assumption plausibility directly.

steps.title: Obtain the distribution view on channel fit and producer appetite
sop: Ask distribution to comment on channel fit and expected producer appetite.
Request comment on whether the target market is reachable through current channels.
Collect the response in writing referencing the brief version.
Done when a written distribution view on channel fit is returned.
verify: Read the distribution response for channel fit and appetite comments.
Pass when both topics are addressed in the response.

steps.title: Log every feedback item in a single disposition log
sop: Transcribe each comment into a log with reviewer, function, and brief section.
Assign an accept, reject, or defer disposition with a written rationale.
Chase any function that has not returned feedback by the deadline.
Done when every received comment carries a disposition and rationale.
verify: Filter the log for items with no disposition.
Pass when no feedback item is left undispositioned.

steps.title: Revise the brief and highlight the changes
sop: Apply the accepted feedback to the brief and increment the version.
Highlight or track the changes so reviewers can see what moved.
Add a change summary listing each change and the feedback that drove it.
Done when the revised version carries highlighted changes and a change summary.
verify: Compare the change summary against the accepted feedback items.
Pass when every accepted item appears in the change summary.

steps.title: Reissue the revised brief to all reviewers
sop: Send the revised version to every reviewer who provided feedback.
Include the disposition log so rejected items and rationale are visible.
File the revised brief and log in the opportunity folder.
Done when the revised brief and log are reissued and filed.
verify: Check the reissue record covers every original reviewer.
Pass when no reviewer is omitted from the reissue.

generic.Defined scope/population: The survey sample frame and achieved respondent set used to validate the qualitative hypotheses at scale.
generic.In-scope period: The fielding window from survey launch to close, with the response cut-off date recorded.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Sample frame, target response count, achieved responses, completion rate, and exclusion count are recorded.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Achieved responses plus screened-out respondents equals the total survey starts recorded in the CRM.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Survey instrument version, fielding dates, and response dataset retained with the extract timestamp.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Segments falling short of minimum sample logged with the decision to extend fielding or qualify findings.
generic.Test population: Every survey response record in the analysis dataset for the fielding window.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any segment falls below its minimum sample size or a direct identifier appears in the analysis dataset.
generic.Exception handling path: Under-sampled segments trigger extended fielding or an explicit caveat on findings from that segment.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Fielding is accepted when the response count and completion rate are recorded against the target.
generic.Evidence location: CRM survey records, the warehouse response dataset, and the Excel analysis workbook.

steps.title: Define the sample frame and target response counts
sop: Define the sample frame from CRM customer and prospect records in scope.
Set the target response count per segment from the minimum sample requirement.
Record the frame definition and targets before fielding starts.
Done when the sample frame and per-segment targets are documented.
verify: Compare the frame definition date against the fielding start date.
Pass when the frame and targets were set before fielding.

steps.title: Map survey questions to the qualitative hypotheses
sop: List each qualitative hypothesis to be validated.
Map each hypothesis to the survey question that tests it.
Remove questions that test no hypothesis and add any missing question.
Done when every hypothesis maps to a survey question and back.
verify: Check the mapping for hypotheses with no question and questions with no hypothesis.
Pass when the mapping is one-to-one with no orphans.

steps.title: Configure screening logic and exclusion capture
sop: Build screening questions that exclude ineligible respondents at the start.
Configure the survey to record the count and reason for each exclusion.
Test the screening logic with pilot responses before launch.
Done when screening logic works and exclusion counts are captured.
verify: Run pilot responses through the screening path.
Pass when ineligible pilots are excluded and counted.

steps.title: Field the survey and monitor response volumes
sop: Launch the survey to the defined sample frame from the CRM.
Monitor daily response volumes against the per-segment targets.
Extend fielding or boost invitations where a segment lags.
Done when fielding closes with responses recorded per segment.
verify: Compare achieved responses per segment against targets.
Pass when every segment meets its minimum or is flagged for caveat.

steps.title: Separate respondent personal data from the analysis dataset
sop: Split respondent contact and identity fields into a restricted linkage file.
Load only the de-identified responses into the warehouse analysis dataset.
Restrict access to the linkage file to the research group.
Done when the analysis dataset carries no direct identifier.
verify: Scan the analysis dataset columns for identifier fields.
Pass when no direct customer identifier is present.

steps.title: Record achieved responses, completion rate, and exclusions
sop: Record the achieved response count, completion rate, and exclusion count.
Reconcile completions plus exclusions plus drop-outs against total starts.
Document any segment falling short with the caveat to apply.
Done when the fielding statistics are recorded and reconciled.
verify: Sum completions, exclusions, and drop-outs against total starts.
Pass when the components reconcile to the recorded starts.

generic.Defined scope/population: The planned customer and broker discovery interviews across the target segments for the opportunity.
generic.In-scope period: The fieldwork window from first interview to final note filing, with consent periods recorded.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each interview record carries date, participant type, segment, consent status, and note location.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Completed interview count equals the planned count per segment or the shortfall is explained.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Interview notes filed in SharePoint tagged with opportunity ID and interview date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Interviews cancelled or refused logged with the replacement participant or the coverage gap accepted.
generic.Test population: Every completed interview in the fieldwork window and its associated note and consent record.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any recorded interview lacks a consent record or any recording is retained beyond the consent period.
generic.Exception handling path: Missing consent invalidates the recording, which is deleted and the interview reported as notes only.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Interviews are accepted when notes exist for every completed interview with a consent record.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint interview notes folder under the opportunity ID plus CRM participant records.

steps.title: Recruit participants from the CRM against the segment quotas
sop: Select candidate customers and brokers from the CRM matching the recruitment criteria.
Cover each target segment and include both retained and lapsed customers.
Record the invited and confirmed participant list against the quotas.
Done when confirmed participants cover every target segment quota.
verify: Compare confirmed participants per segment against the quota table.
Pass when every quota is met or the shortfall is logged.

steps.title: Capture recorded consent before each interview
sop: Read the privacy notice and consent wording to each participant.
Capture explicit consent for recording or transcription where used.
Record the consent status and the consent retention period.
Done when every recorded interview has a captured consent record.
verify: Match consent records against the interviews marked as recorded.
Pass when no recorded interview lacks a consent record.

steps.title: Run the interviews using the approved interview guide
sop: Conduct each interview over Teams using the approved guide.
Follow the guide sequence so responses stay comparable across interviews.
Probe on unexpected answers without leading the participant.
Done when every scheduled interview has been conducted.
verify: Compare completed interviews against the schedule.
Pass when every scheduled interview is completed or its cancellation is logged.

steps.title: Capture verbatim quotes in the interview notes
sop: Record verbatim quotes alongside the interviewer summary for each theme.
Mark clearly which text is verbatim and which is paraphrase.
Avoid notes that contain only interviewer interpretation.
Done when every interview note contains verbatim quotes.
verify: Sample interview notes for verbatim sections.
Pass when each sampled note contains marked verbatim quotes.

steps.title: Tag and file each note under the opportunity ID
sop: Name each note file with the opportunity ID, participant type, and interview date.
File the notes in the SharePoint interview folder for the opportunity.
Link the interview record in the CRM to the note location.
Done when every note is filed and tagged to the opportunity ID.
verify: Search SharePoint by opportunity ID for the interview notes.
Pass when a note is returned for every completed interview.

steps.title: Dispose of recordings at the end of the consent period
sop: List recordings with their consent retention end dates.
Delete each recording once its consent period expires.
Record the deletion date against the interview record.
Done when no recording is retained past its consent period.
verify: Check the recording store against the consent expiry dates.
Pass when no recording remains beyond its stated consent period.

generic.Defined scope/population: The voice-of-customer research plan covering research questions, instruments, recruitment criteria, and consent wording.

generic.Required fields populated and valid: Research questions, decisions informed, quotas, instruments, privacy notice, and incentives are all documented.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Recruitment quota counts across segments sum to the planned total sample size.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Plan versioned in SharePoint with attached interview guide and survey instrument and the approval date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Research questions with no feasible method logged with the alternative approach or the decision to drop.
generic.Test population: Every research question, quota, and instrument in the approved plan.

generic.Exception handling path: Missing instruments or quotas block approval until attached and completed.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The plan is accepted when approved with instruments attached and quotas set before fieldwork.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint research plan folder holding the plan, guide, instrument, and approval record.

steps.title: State the research questions and the decisions they inform
sop: List the research questions the study must answer.
Name the product decision each question will inform.
Drop questions that inform no decision.
Done when every research question names the decision it informs.
verify: Filter the question list for blank decision references.
Pass when no research question lacks a named decision.

steps.title: Draft and attach the interview guide
sop: Draft the interview guide covering each research question.
Order questions so early answers do not lead later ones.
Attach the guide file to the plan rather than referencing it.
Done when the interview guide is drafted and attached to the plan.
verify: Open the plan and check the guide attachment.
Pass when the guide is attached and covers every research question.

steps.title: Draft and attach the survey instrument
sop: Draft the survey instrument mapping to the same research questions.
Include screening questions and response scales.
Attach the instrument file to the plan.
Done when the survey instrument is drafted and attached.
verify: Open the plan and check the instrument attachment.
Pass when the instrument is attached and maps to the research questions.

steps.title: Set recruitment quotas by segment, tenure, and channel
sop: Set target counts by customer segment, tenure band, and distribution channel.
Check the quota totals sum to the planned sample size.
Record the quotas in an Excel quota table attached to the plan.
Done when quotas are set and sum to the planned sample.
verify: Sum the quota table against the planned total sample size.
Pass when the quota totals reconcile to the planned sample.

steps.title: Include the privacy notice and consent wording
sop: Insert the privacy notice and consent wording participants will be given.
Confirm the wording covers recording, retention, and use of responses.
Attach the approved wording to the plan.
Done when the privacy notice and consent wording are included in the plan.
verify: Read the plan for the privacy and consent section.
Pass when both the privacy notice and consent wording are present.

steps.title: Describe and clear any participant incentives
sop: Describe any incentive offered to participants and its value.
Check the incentive against the conflicts of interest standard.
Record the clearance outcome in the plan.
Done when incentives are described and cleared or confirmed as none.
verify: Read the incentive section and its clearance record.
Pass when incentives are either cleared or explicitly stated as none.

steps.title: Obtain plan approval before fieldwork begins
sop: Submit the plan with attachments for approval.
Record the approver name and approval date.
Hold fieldwork until approval is recorded.
Done when the plan is approved and dated before fieldwork starts.
verify: Compare the approval date against the fieldwork start date.
Pass when approval precedes the fieldwork start.

generic.Defined scope/population: The alignment workshop on research implications with product, underwriting, actuarial, distribution, and operations.

generic.Required fields populated and valid: Pre-read date, attendance by function, accepted findings, disputed findings, and follow-up owners are recorded.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Findings marked accepted plus findings marked disputed equals the total findings presented.

generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Disputed findings logged with a named follow-up owner and a resolution date.
generic.Test population: Every research finding tabled at the workshop and every function invited.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any disputed finding has no follow-up owner or a required function is unrepresented.
generic.Exception handling path: Unrepresented functions are given a catch-up session and their input recorded before outcomes are final.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The workshop is accepted when attendance and captured outcomes are recorded with owned follow-ups.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint workshop folder holding the pack, attendance list, and outcome note.

steps.title: Circulate the research synthesis pack as pre-read
sop: Assemble the synthesis pack with the findings to be discussed.
Send it to invitees ahead of the workshop with the pre-read deadline stated.
Save the pack and the circulation record to the workshop folder.
Done when the pack is circulated ahead of the workshop.
verify: Compare the circulation timestamp against the workshop date.
Pass when the pack was circulated before the workshop.

steps.title: Confirm attendance covers all five functions
sop: Invite named representatives from product, underwriting, actuarial, distribution, and operations.
Chase any function with no confirmed attendee before the session.
Record substitutes where a named attendee cannot attend.
Done when every required function has a confirmed attendee.
verify: Check the confirmed attendee list against the five required functions.
Pass when each function has at least one confirmed attendee.

steps.title: Facilitate the session finding by finding
sop: Take each research finding in turn and invite challenge.
Ask the group to mark each finding accepted or disputed.
Prevent the session moving on with a finding unclassified.
Done when every finding is marked accepted or disputed.
verify: Count accepted plus disputed findings against the findings presented.
Pass when the totals reconcile with no unclassified finding.

steps.title: Assign follow-up owners to disputed findings
sop: For each disputed finding agree what evidence would settle the dispute.
Assign a named owner and a resolution date to obtain that evidence.
Record the dispute and the follow-up in the outcome note.
Done when every disputed finding has an owner and a resolution date.
verify: Filter disputed findings for blank owners or dates.
Pass when no disputed finding lacks a follow-up owner and date.

steps.title: Write down the agreed implications before the session closes
sop: Capture the agreed implication for the product concept from each accepted finding.
Read the implications back to the group for confirmation in session.
Correct any implication the group does not accept as stated.
Done when the agreed implications are written and confirmed in session.
verify: Compare the implication list against the accepted findings.
Pass when every accepted finding has a confirmed implication.

steps.title: Issue and file the attendance list and outcome note
sop: Export the Teams attendance list at the end of the session.
Compile the outcome note covering accepted, disputed, and implications.
File both in the SharePoint workshop folder and issue to attendees.
Done when attendance and outcomes are filed and issued.
verify: Retrieve the workshop folder from a non-author account.
Pass when the attendance list and outcome note are both present.

generic.Defined scope/population: The internal and external stakeholder register for the product opportunity across all affected functions.
generic.In-scope period: The opportunity lifecycle from intake to design handover, with the register reviewed each stage.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each row carries name, role, organisation, internal or external flag, engagement mode, frequency, and relationship owner.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Function coverage count equals the required function list with no required function missing a representative.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Register saved in SharePoint under the opportunity ID with a version and last review date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Functions without an identified representative logged with the escalation and the date resolved.
generic.Test population: Every stakeholder row in the register and every required function on the coverage list.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any stakeholder row lacks an engagement mode or owner, or a required function is unrepresented.
generic.Exception handling path: Unrepresented functions are escalated to the function lead for nomination before the register is baselined.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The register is accepted when filed under the opportunity ID with complete rows for all required functions.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint opportunity folder stakeholder register workbook.

steps.title: List the required internal functions for coverage
sop: List underwriting, actuarial, claims, distribution, compliance, and IT as required functions.
Add any further function the opportunity scope makes relevant.
Record the coverage list as the checklist for the register.
Done when the required function coverage list is agreed.
verify: Compare the coverage list against the opportunity scope.
Pass when every function affected by the opportunity appears.

steps.title: Identify a named representative per internal function
sop: Obtain a named representative from each required function.
Record name, role, and organisation unit for each representative.
Escalate to the function lead where no representative is nominated.
Done when every required function has a named representative or an escalation.
verify: Check the register against the coverage list.
Pass when no required function is left without a representative or escalation.

steps.title: Add relevant external stakeholders to the register
sop: Identify brokers, reinsurers, and key partners relevant to the opportunity.
Record each with the internal or external flag set correctly.
Exclude external parties with no material interest in the opportunity.
Done when relevant external stakeholders are recorded and flagged.
verify: Filter the register by the external flag and review the entries.
Pass when the external entries are relevant and correctly flagged.

steps.title: Record engagement mode and frequency per stakeholder
sop: Set the engagement mode such as workshop, review, or information only.
Set the engagement frequency appropriate to the stakeholder influence.
Avoid leaving mode or frequency blank on any row.
Done when every stakeholder has an engagement mode and frequency.
verify: Filter the register for blank mode or frequency cells.
Pass when no stakeholder row is missing either field.

steps.title: Name the relationship owner for each external stakeholder
sop: Name the internal person who owns each external relationship.
Confirm each named owner accepts the relationship ownership.
Record the owner name against the external stakeholder row.
Done when every external stakeholder has a named relationship owner.
verify: Filter external rows for blank relationship owners.
Pass when no external stakeholder is left without an owner.

steps.title: Version and file the register under the opportunity ID
sop: Version the register workbook and set the last review date.
Save it to the SharePoint opportunity folder using the opportunity ID.
Notify the opportunity owner that the register is available.
Done when the versioned register is filed under the opportunity ID.
verify: Search SharePoint by the opportunity ID from a non-author account.
Pass when the current stakeholder register is returned.

generic.Defined scope/population: The product concept brief revised to reflect voice-of-customer research findings ahead of the design phase.
generic.In-scope period: The revision window between research synthesis completion and the design stage gate.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Version number, change summary, finding citations, target market update, and hypothesis status are populated.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Change summary entry count equals the count of substantive changes made to the brief.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Revised brief versioned in SharePoint with full version history retained and mirrored on Confluence.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Findings not reflected in the brief logged with the rationale for not actioning them.
generic.Test population: Every substantive change in the revised brief and every hypothesis affected by research.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any prior brief version is deleted from history or a change has no cited research finding.
generic.Exception handling path: Uncited changes are either given a finding citation or reverted before the brief is reissued.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The revision is accepted when the incremented version carries a change summary citing research findings.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint opportunity folder brief version history and the Confluence opportunity page.

steps.title: Collect the research findings that affect the brief
sop: List the validated needs, personas, and preference rankings from the synthesis.
Identify which brief sections each finding affects.
Record the finding identifiers so the brief can cite them.
Done when the affecting findings are listed with brief section references.
verify: Check each listed finding names the brief section it affects.
Pass when no finding is listed without a target section.

steps.title: Apply changes to the brief with finding citations
sop: Edit each affected brief section using the research finding.
Cite the finding identifier alongside each substantive change.
Avoid making changes that no finding supports.
Done when every substantive change carries a finding citation.
verify: Scan the changed sections for uncited edits.
Pass when no substantive change is uncited.

steps.title: Update the target market section where research changed it
sop: Compare the researched segment view against the brief target market.
Update the target market and out-of-scope statements where research diverges.
Cite the finding that changed the segment view.
Done when the target market reflects the researched segment view.
verify: Compare the brief target market against the synthesis segments.
Pass when the two are consistent or the difference is explained.

steps.title: Mark disproved hypotheses rather than deleting them
sop: Identify hypotheses the research disproved.
Mark each as disproved with the evidence that disproved it.
Keep the disproved hypothesis text in the brief for traceability.
Done when every disproved hypothesis is marked and retained.
verify: Search the brief for the original hypothesis text.
Pass when disproved hypotheses remain present and marked.

steps.title: Increment the version and write the change summary
sop: Increment the brief version number.
Write a change summary listing each change and the finding behind it.
Check the prior version remains available in the version history.
Done when the version is incremented with a change summary.
verify: Open the SharePoint version history for the brief.
Pass when prior versions remain and the new version carries a change summary.

steps.title: Reissue the revised brief before the design stage gate
sop: Send the revised brief to the design team and the original reviewers.
Update the Confluence opportunity page to point at the new version.
Confirm the reissue happens before the design stage gate date.
Done when the revised brief is reissued ahead of the gate.
verify: Compare the reissue date against the design stage gate date.
Pass when the reissue precedes the gate.

generic.Defined scope/population: The traceability record linking every product decision in the decision log to its supporting research finding.
generic.In-scope period: The research and decision window for the opportunity up to the stage-gate pack assembly.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each row carries decision ID, decision text, linked finding ID, link type, and rationale where unlinked.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Decision count in the traceability record equals the decision count in the decision log.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Traceability record stored with the concept brief in Confluence and the requirements repository with a version.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Material findings not linked to a decision logged as not actioned with a rationale.
generic.Test population: Every product decision row and every material research finding for the opportunity.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any decision has no linked finding or any material finding has neither a link nor a rationale.
generic.Exception handling path: Decisions made against the evidence are flagged and justified rather than left unexplained.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Traceability is accepted when every decision links to a finding and artifacts are referenced by ID.
generic.Evidence location: Confluence traceability page plus the requirements repository records it references.

steps.title: Extract the decision log for the opportunity
sop: Pull the product decision log for the opportunity into Excel.
Record decision ID, decision text, decision maker, and date.
Confirm the log covers all decisions taken in the research stage.
Done when the full decision population is extracted.
verify: Compare the extract count against the decision log entry count.
Pass when all decisions are present in the extract.

steps.title: Extract the material research findings
sop: List the material findings from the synthesis with their finding identifiers.
Exclude minor observations that do not bear on any decision.
Record the artifact ID or link for each finding.
Done when material findings are listed with identifiers and artifact links.
verify: Check every listed finding carries an identifier and artifact link.
Pass when no finding is listed by title alone.

steps.title: Link each decision to its supporting finding
sop: For each decision record the finding identifier that supports it.
Where several findings apply record each link separately.
Reference findings by ID or link rather than by title.
Done when every decision carries at least one finding link.
verify: Filter the traceability record for decisions with no finding link.
Pass when no decision row is unlinked.

steps.title: Flag decisions made against the research evidence
sop: Identify decisions that run counter to the linked research finding.
Flag each and record the justification for deciding against the evidence.
Escalate flagged decisions to the opportunity owner for confirmation.
Done when every counter-evidence decision is flagged and justified.
verify: Read the flagged decisions for a recorded justification.
Pass when no counter-evidence decision is left unjustified.

steps.title: Mark unactioned findings with a rationale
sop: Identify material findings that link to no decision.
Mark each as not actioned with the rationale for not acting.
Escalate any finding that should have driven a decision.
Done when every unlinked material finding carries a rationale.
verify: Filter findings for those with neither a decision link nor a rationale.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Publish the traceability record with the concept brief
sop: Publish the traceability record to Confluence alongside the concept brief.
Reference the requirements repository records for each linked requirement.
Include the record in the stage-gate pack contents list.
Done when the record is published with the brief and in the gate pack.
verify: Open the Confluence brief page and follow the traceability link.
Pass when the traceability record resolves and references artifacts by ID.

generic.Defined scope/population: All customer research studies held in the research repository for the current cycle plus prior retained studies.
generic.In-scope period: The current research cycle for new entries and the full retention window for disposition review.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each repository entry carries study date, method, segment, access class, and retention disposal date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Repository entry count for the cycle equals the completed study count on the research plan.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Studies retained in the document management repository with upload timestamps and superseded markers.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Studies past retention logged with the disposition applied and the approver of that disposition.
generic.Test population: Every study entry in the research repository including superseded and retention-expired entries.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any entry lacks date, method, or segment metadata or any study past retention is undispositioned.
generic.Exception handling path: Retention-expired studies are dispositioned per schedule with the approval recorded before closure.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The repository is accepted when metadata is complete and retention dispositions are current.
generic.Evidence location: Document management repository research library plus the SharePoint research index.

steps.title: List studies completed this cycle
sop: List every research study completed in the current cycle.
Record author, completion date, method, and segments covered.
Confirm the list with the research authors.
Done when the completed study list is agreed.
verify: Compare the study list against the research plan deliverables.
Pass when every planned study appears or its cancellation is noted.

steps.title: Create repository entries with full metadata
sop: Create a repository entry for each completed study.
Populate date, method, segment, and product line metadata fields.
Attach the study file to the entry.
Done when every completed study has a metadata-complete entry.
verify: Filter repository entries for blank date, method, or segment.
Pass when no entry is missing any of the three fields.

steps.title: Mark superseded research rather than deleting it
sop: Identify studies replaced by newer research this cycle.
Mark each as superseded and link it to the replacing study.
Leave the superseded study in the repository.
Done when superseded studies are marked and linked.
verify: Search the repository for the superseded study titles.
Pass when superseded studies remain present and are labelled.

steps.title: Restrict access to studies containing personal data
sop: Identify studies whose files retain personal data.
Set access on those entries to the research group only.
Record the access class applied on the entry metadata.
Done when personal-data studies are restricted to the research group.
verify: Attempt to open a restricted study from an account outside the research group.
Pass when access is denied for the non-research account.

steps.title: Test repository search by segment and product line
sop: Search the repository by segment and by product line for a sample of studies.
Confirm each sampled study is returned by both searches.
Correct metadata where a study is not returned.
Done when sampled studies are retrievable by segment and product line.
verify: Re-run both searches after any metadata correction.
Pass when every sampled study is returned by both queries.

steps.title: Disposition studies past their retention date
sop: List studies whose retention disposal date has passed.
Apply the disposition required by the retention schedule.
Record the disposition action, date, and approver on the entry.
Done when no study past retention is left undispositioned.
verify: Filter the repository for entries past retention with no disposition.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

generic.Defined scope/population: The research findings pack presented to the product owner and underwriting leadership for interpretation.
generic.In-scope period: The review session date and the research window the findings cover.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each headline finding carries a sample size, method, and the segment it applies to.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Sample sizes quoted in the pack reconcile to the response counts in the research dataset.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Findings pack, meeting record, and Power BI report version retained in SharePoint with the session date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Interpretation disagreements minuted with the follow-up owner and resolution route.
generic.Test population: Every headline finding in the pack and every required attendee for the session.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any headline finding is presented without its sample size or a required attendee is absent.
generic.Exception handling path: Absent required attendees are given a catch-up briefing recorded before conclusions are acted on.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The review is accepted when the meeting record shows attendees and agreed next steps with owners.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint research review folder plus the Power BI findings report used in the session.

steps.title: Build the findings pack with sample size per finding
sop: State each headline finding with its sample size, method, and segment.
Reconcile the sample sizes against the research response dataset.
Remove any finding whose sample size cannot be stated.
Done when every headline finding carries a reconciled sample size.
verify: Compare pack sample sizes against the dataset counts.
Pass when every quoted sample size matches the dataset.

steps.title: Publish the supporting views in Power BI
sop: Build the Power BI report views that evidence each headline finding.
Confirm each view filters to the segment stated in the finding.
Share the report with the session attendees before the meeting.
Done when the Power BI views are published and shared.
verify: Open each Power BI view and check its segment filter.
Pass when every view matches the finding it evidences.

steps.title: Include findings that challenge the concept direction
sop: Identify findings that contradict the current concept direction.
Include them in the pack with equal prominence to supportive findings.
Avoid filtering out inconvenient findings from the presentation.
Done when challenging findings are present in the pack.
verify: Compare the pack findings against the full synthesis finding list.
Pass when no material challenging finding is omitted.

steps.title: Hold the session with the product owner and underwriting leader
sop: Convene the session over Teams with the product owner and an underwriting leader.
Present each finding and invite interpretation from both attendees.
Record attendance from the Teams participant list.
Done when the session is held with both required roles present.
verify: Check the attendance record for the product owner and underwriting leader.
Pass when both are recorded as attending.

steps.title: Minute interpretation disagreements
sop: Record any disagreement over what a finding means.
Note the competing interpretations and who holds each.
Assign a route to resolve the disagreement with an owner.
Done when every disagreement is minuted with a resolution route.
verify: Read the meeting record for the disagreements section.
Pass when disagreements are recorded with owners rather than omitted.

steps.title: Capture agreed next steps with owners before the session ends
sop: List the next steps agreed during the session.
Assign each a named owner and a due date agreed in the meeting.
Read the list back for confirmation before closing the session.
Done when next steps are captured with owners and confirmed in session.
verify: Filter the next steps list for blank owners or dates.
Pass when every next step carries an owner and a due date.

generic.Defined scope/population: The synthesised set of validated customer needs, pain points, personas, and preference rankings from the VoC research.
generic.In-scope period: The research window covering the interviews and surveys feeding the synthesis.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each need carries evidence sources, each persona a segment size, and each ranking a question and respondent count.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Persona segment sizes reconcile to the warehouse customer counts for the same segment definitions.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Synthesis workbook versioned in SharePoint with the research dataset extract date recorded.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Needs supported by only one source logged as provisional with the further evidence required.
generic.Test population: Every validated need, persona, pain point, and preference ranking in the synthesis.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any need lacks two independent evidence sources or any persona has no underlying segment size.
generic.Exception handling path: Single-source needs are marked provisional and excluded from the validated set until corroborated.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The synthesis is accepted when every validated need has a populated evidence-source column.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint synthesis workbook plus the warehouse dataset holding survey and interview evidence.

steps.title: Consolidate interview and survey evidence in the warehouse
