sop: Load the de-identified interview themes and survey responses into the warehouse dataset.
Record the extract date and the source study identifiers.
Confirm the dataset carries no direct customer identifier.
Done when the consolidated evidence dataset is loaded and dated.
verify: Scan the dataset columns for identifier fields.
Pass when no direct identifier is present in the consolidated dataset.

steps.title: Validate each need against two independent sources
sop: For each candidate need identify the independent sources supporting it.
Promote needs with two or more independent sources to validated.
Mark single-source needs as provisional with the evidence required.
Done when every need is classified validated or provisional.
verify: Filter validated needs for those with fewer than two sources.
Pass when no validated need rests on a single source.

steps.title: Rank pain points by frequency and severity
sop: Score each pain point for frequency using the observation counts.
Score severity using the agreed severity scale.
Rank pain points using the combined score formula.
Done when every pain point is scored and ranked on the stated scale.
verify: Check the ranking recalculates from the frequency and severity columns.
Pass when the rank order follows the formula, not manual ordering.

steps.title: Build personas from observed data with segment sizes
sop: Build each persona from observed behaviours and attributes in the dataset.
Attach the segment size from the warehouse customer counts.
Reject personas that cannot be tied to observed data.
Done when every persona carries an observed basis and a segment size.
verify: Filter personas for blank segment size values.
Pass when no persona is presented without an underlying segment size.

steps.title: Report preference rankings with question and respondent count
sop: State the survey question behind each preference ranking.
State the number of respondents who answered that question.
Avoid reporting a ranking without its base.
Done when every preference ranking states its question and base.
verify: Filter ranking rows for blank question or respondent count.
Pass when no ranking is reported without both fields.

steps.title: Retain findings contradicting the original hypothesis
sop: Identify findings that contradict the opportunity hypothesis.
Keep them in the synthesis with the same evidence treatment as supportive findings.
Flag the hypothesis elements the contradicting findings challenge.
Done when contradicting findings are retained and flagged.
verify: Compare the synthesis findings against the raw evidence themes.
Pass when no contradicting theme has been dropped from the synthesis.

steps.title: Version and publish the synthesis to SharePoint
sop: Complete the evidence-source column for every validated need.
Version the synthesis workbook and record the dataset extract date.
Publish it to the SharePoint research folder for the opportunity.
Done when the versioned synthesis is published with complete evidence sources.
verify: Open the published workbook and filter for blank evidence-source cells.
Pass when no validated need has a blank evidence source.

generic.Defined scope/population: The product feature requirements and coverage specifications derived from validated customer insights.
generic.In-scope period: The requirements definition stage between research synthesis and the design stage gate.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each requirement carries a unique ID, linked customer need, limits, exclusions, and compliance flag where relevant.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Requirement count in the repository equals the count in the approved requirements baseline.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Requirements versioned in the requirements repository and mirrored on the Confluence requirements page.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Requirements not supported by research marked as assumptions with a validation owner and date.
generic.Test population: Every requirement row in the requirements repository for this product concept.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any requirement has no unique ID or linked need, or any coverage requirement omits limits and exclusions.
generic.Exception handling path: Unsupported requirements are marked as assumptions rather than deleted, and routed for validation.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Requirements are accepted when each has a unique ID and a linked customer need.
generic.Evidence location: Requirements repository records plus the Confluence requirements page and SharePoint source synthesis.

steps.title: Load the validated needs into the requirements repository
sop: Import the validated need identifiers and statements from the synthesis.
Create the need reference list in the requirements repository.
Confirm the imported set matches the validated needs in the synthesis.
Done when the validated needs are available for linking in the repository.
verify: Compare the imported need count against the synthesis validated need count.
Pass when the counts match.

steps.title: Write feature requirements with unique IDs
sop: Write each feature requirement as a single testable statement.
Let the repository assign a unique requirement ID to each.
Avoid combining several requirements into one statement.
Done when every requirement exists with a unique ID.
verify: Run a duplicate check on requirement IDs and statements.
Pass when every requirement has a unique ID and single scope.

steps.title: Link each requirement to the customer need it satisfies
sop: Set the linked need identifier on each requirement.
Where a requirement satisfies several needs record each link.
Flag requirements that link to no validated need.
Done when every requirement carries a need link or a flag.
verify: Filter requirements for a blank linked need.
Pass when no requirement is unlinked and unflagged.

steps.title: Specify limits, sub-limits, deductibles, and exclusions
sop: For each coverage requirement state limits, sub-limits, and deductibles.
State the intended exclusions explicitly rather than by omission.
Write the specification so underwriting and actuarial can rate against it.
Done when every coverage requirement states limits and exclusions.
verify: Filter coverage requirements for missing limits or exclusions.
Pass when no coverage requirement lacks either.

steps.title: Flag requirements implying a regulatory obligation
sop: Review requirements for disclosure, suitability, or product governance implications.
Set the compliance review flag on each such requirement.
Route flagged requirements to Compliance for review with a due date.
Done when every regulatory-implicating requirement is flagged and routed.
verify: Check the Compliance review queue against the flagged requirements.
Pass when every flagged requirement is in the review queue.

steps.title: Mark unsupported requirements as assumptions
sop: Identify requirements the research does not support.
Mark each as an assumption with a validation owner and target date.
Keep assumptions visible rather than presenting them as evidenced.
Done when unsupported requirements are marked as assumptions with owners.
verify: Filter assumption-marked requirements for blank validation owners.
Pass when every assumption carries a validation owner and date.

steps.title: Publish the requirements baseline to Confluence
sop: Baseline the requirement set in the repository with a version.
Publish the requirements page in Confluence referencing repository IDs.
Save a snapshot to the SharePoint opportunity folder for the gate pack.
Done when the baselined requirements are published and snapshotted.
verify: Open the Confluence page and follow a sample of requirement ID links.
Pass when the links resolve to the repository records.

generic.Defined scope/population: The feature requirements validated with distribution partners covering every intended distribution channel.
generic.In-scope period: The partner validation window from requirement circulation to disposition of all partner feedback.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each feedback row carries partner, channel, requirement ID, comment, and disposition.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Channels with recorded partner feedback equal the intended distribution channel list.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Partner feedback logged in the CRM and filed in SharePoint against the requirement version reviewed.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Requirements partners flag as unsaleable logged with a keep, change, or drop decision and rationale.
generic.Test population: Every requirement reviewed by partners and every intended distribution channel.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any partner-flagged unsaleable requirement is left undispositioned or a channel has no feedback.
generic.Exception handling path: Channels without partner feedback are escalated to the channel owner before requirements are baselined.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Validation is accepted when logged partner feedback exists against the product requirements for every channel.
generic.Evidence location: CRM partner interaction records plus the SharePoint validation folder feedback log.

steps.title: Identify partners covering each intended channel
sop: List the intended distribution channels for the product.
Select at least one partner per channel from the CRM partner records.
Confirm each selected partner is active and appropriate to consult.
Done when every intended channel has a nominated partner.
verify: Compare nominated partners against the intended channel list.
Pass when no channel is left without a nominated partner.

steps.title: Circulate the requirements to nominated partners
sop: Send the requirement summary with limits, exclusions, and indicative price point.
State the specific questions partners should answer.
Set a response deadline and record the circulation in the CRM.
Done when every nominated partner has the requirements and a deadline.
verify: Check the CRM circulation records against the partner list.
Pass when every nominated partner has a circulation record.

steps.title: Obtain comment on price point, commission, and ease of quote
sop: Ask partners to comment specifically on price point and commission viability.
Ask whether the product can be quoted easily in their workflow.
Chase partners who respond without addressing these topics.
Done when each partner response covers all three topics.
verify: Read each response for the three required topics.
Pass when no partner response omits price, commission, or ease of quote.

steps.title: Compare partner target market views against the brief
sop: Extract each partner view on who would buy the product.
Compare it against the target market documented in the concept brief.
Record divergences for resolution before requirements are baselined.
Done when every partner target market view is compared to the brief.
verify: Read the comparison record for unexplained divergences.
Pass when every divergence is recorded with a resolution route.

steps.title: Disposition unsaleable requirement flags
sop: List each requirement partners flagged as unsaleable.
Decide to keep, change, or drop each with a written rationale.
Record the decision maker and date against each flagged requirement.
Done when every unsaleable flag carries a documented decision.
verify: Filter flagged requirements for blank decisions.
Pass when no unsaleable flag is left undispositioned.

steps.title: Version-track requirements changed by partner feedback
sop: Apply agreed changes to the requirements and increment the version.
Record the partner feedback reference against each change.
File the feedback log and revised requirements in SharePoint.
Done when changed requirements are version-tracked with feedback references.
verify: Open the requirement version history for a sample of changed requirements.
Pass when each change is traceable to a partner feedback item.

generic.Defined scope/population: All concepts screened out at the current screening cycle and their archived rationale records.
generic.In-scope period: The screening cycle in which the concepts were rejected, with decision dates recorded.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each archived concept carries rejection rationale, failed criterion, decision maker, decision date, and status.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Screened-out concept count in the archive equals the screened-out count in the pipeline register.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Archived concepts retained in the document management repository with archive timestamp and rationale attached.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Concepts rejected for temporary reasons tagged for reconsideration with a review date.
generic.Test population: Every concept marked screened out in the current screening cycle.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any screened-out concept remains in an active pipeline status or lacks a rejection rationale.
generic.Exception handling path: Concepts left in review status are corrected to screened-out with the decision record attached.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Archiving is accepted when rationale and decision date are stored with every archived concept.
generic.Evidence location: PPM tool pipeline register status plus the document management repository archive folder.

steps.title: Extract screened-out concepts from the pipeline register
sop: Run the pipeline register report filtered to the current screening cycle.
Identify concepts with a screening decision of reject.
Export the list with concept ID, decision date, and current status.
Done when the screened-out concept list is extracted.
verify: Compare the extract count against the screening scorecard reject count.
Pass when the two counts agree.

steps.title: Write the rejection rationale naming the failed criterion
sop: For each concept record which screening criterion it failed.
Write a rationale explaining why the concept failed that criterion.
Avoid generic rationales that do not name a criterion.
Done when every screened-out concept has a criterion-specific rationale.
verify: Read each rationale for a named failed criterion.
Pass when no rationale omits the failed criterion.

steps.title: Record the decision maker and decision date
sop: Record the name of the decision maker who rejected each concept.
Record the decision date from the screening meeting record.
Correct any concept where the decision record is missing.
Done when every archived concept carries a decision maker and date.
verify: Filter the archive list for blank decision maker or date.
Pass when no archived concept is missing either field.

steps.title: Set the pipeline register status to screened-out
sop: Update each concept status in the PPM tool to screened-out.
Confirm no rejected concept remains in review or active status.
Record the status change date in the register history.
Done when every rejected concept shows screened-out status.
verify: Run the register report for active-status concepts with a reject decision.
Pass when the report returns no rows.

steps.title: Tag temporary rejections for reconsideration
sop: Identify concepts rejected for a temporary reason such as capacity or timing.
Tag each for reconsideration and set a review date.
Record the condition that would make the concept viable again.
Done when every temporary rejection carries a reconsideration tag and date.
verify: Filter temporary rejections for a blank review date.
Pass when every temporary rejection has a review date.

steps.title: Archive concepts to the repository and test searchability
sop: Upload each concept pack and its rationale to the archive folder.
Apply metadata for LOB, segment, and rejection criterion.
Ask a colleague to search the archive by criterion and LOB.
Done when archived concepts are retrievable by search.
verify: Run the archive search from a non-author account.
Pass when every archived concept is returned with its rationale.

generic.Defined scope/population: All shortlisted product concepts assessed for technology, operational, and underwriting feasibility.
generic.In-scope period: The feasibility assessment window before the concept stage-gate review.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each concept carries a rating and rationale for each of the three feasibility dimensions.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Assessed concept count equals the shortlisted concept count in the pipeline register.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Assessment workbook versioned in SharePoint with the policy administration system configuration finding attached.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Red-rated dimensions logged with a mitigation option, estimated cost, and lead time.
generic.Test population: Every shortlisted concept and each of its three feasibility dimensions.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any feasibility dimension is unrated for a shortlisted concept or a red rating has no mitigation.
generic.Exception handling path: Unrated dimensions are referred to the owning function for assessment before the stage gate.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The assessment is accepted when it confirms whether the concept is configurable without custom code.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint feasibility folder workbook plus the policy administration system configuration analysis.

steps.title: Confirm the shortlisted concept population
sop: Pull the shortlisted concepts from the pipeline register.
Create an assessment row per concept in the feasibility workbook.
Confirm the list with the Insurance Product Dev Lead.
Done when every shortlisted concept has an assessment row.
verify: Compare workbook rows against the register shortlist count.
Pass when the counts match.

steps.title: Assess policy administration system configurability
sop: Review each concept against the policy administration system product model.
State whether the product can be configured as designed without custom code.
Record the specific configuration constraint where custom code is required.
Done when configurability is stated for every concept.
verify: Read the technology assessment for an explicit configurability statement.
Pass when every concept states configurable or requires custom code.

steps.title: Assess servicing, billing, and claims operational impacts
sop: Identify servicing, billing, and claims handling impacts for each concept.
Name the operational owner for each impact identified.
Record the change effort each impact implies.
Done when operational impacts are recorded with named owners.
verify: Filter operational impacts for blank owner names.
Pass when every operational impact names an owner.

steps.title: Assess underwriting feasibility and data availability
sop: State whether the risk can be assessed with the data and rating factors available.
Identify missing data or rating factors that would block underwriting.
Record the actuarial view on loss predictability for the concept.
Done when underwriting feasibility is stated for every concept.
verify: Read the underwriting assessment for a data availability statement.
Pass when every concept states whether the risk is assessable.

steps.title: Apply a red, amber, or green rating per dimension
sop: Rate each of the three dimensions red, amber, or green for every concept.
Record the rationale supporting each rating.
Avoid leaving any dimension blank or rated by narrative only.
Done when every dimension carries a rating and rationale.
verify: Filter the workbook for blank rating cells.
Pass when no feasibility dimension is left unrated.

steps.title: Attach a mitigation and cost to every red rating
sop: For each red rating propose a mitigation option.
Estimate the cost or lead time the mitigation would require.
Name the owner accountable for delivering the mitigation.
Done when every red rating has a mitigation with cost or lead time.
verify: Filter red-rated rows for missing mitigation or cost.
Pass when no red rating is left without a mitigation and estimate.

steps.title: Version and file the feasibility assessment
sop: Version the assessment workbook and stamp the assessment date.
File it in the SharePoint feasibility folder for the screening cycle.
Include it in the stage-gate pack contents list.
Done when the versioned assessment is filed and listed in the gate pack.
verify: Open the filed workbook and check ratings and mitigations are intact.
Pass when the filed version is complete and dated.

generic.Defined scope/population: The approved concept and the product development squad assigned to deliver its next stage.
generic.In-scope period: The target delivery period for which the squad capacity is being committed.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Squad name, start date, capacity confirmation, skill coverage, and kick-off date are recorded.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Squad committed effort across assigned concepts does not exceed its stated capacity for the period.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Assignment recorded in the PPM tool and the delivery tool with the assignment timestamp.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Skill or capacity gaps logged with the resourcing action and the date it will be closed.
generic.Test population: The squad assignment record and the squad capacity position for the target period.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if the squad is allocated beyond its stated capacity or the concept has no start date.
generic.Exception handling path: Over-allocated squads trigger a re-plan or an alternative squad before the assignment is confirmed.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Assignment is accepted when the concept is assigned to a named squad with a start date.
generic.Evidence location: PPM tool concept record plus the Jira Align squad allocation and capacity view.

steps.title: Review squad capacity in Jira Align for the target period
sop: Open the Jira Align capacity view for candidate squads in the target period.
Compare committed effort against stated capacity for each squad.
Shortlist squads with headroom for the concept effort estimate.
Done when candidate squads with available capacity are shortlisted.
verify: Read the capacity view for each shortlisted squad.
Pass when each shortlisted squad shows headroom for the concept.

steps.title: Check skill coverage against the concept requirements
sop: List the actuarial, product, and configuration skills the concept needs.
Compare against the skills held in each shortlisted squad.
Log skill gaps with the resourcing action needed to close them.
Done when skill coverage is confirmed or gaps are logged.
verify: Compare the required skill list against the selected squad skill profile.
Pass when every required skill is covered or has a logged action.

steps.title: Confirm capacity acceptance with the squad lead
sop: Send the squad lead the concept scope and effort estimate.
Ask for confirmation that the squad can take it in the target period.
Record the confirmation or the constraint raised.
Done when the squad lead has confirmed or declined capacity.
verify: Read the squad lead confirmation record.
Pass when a written capacity confirmation exists for the target period.

steps.title: Record the assignment with a start date in the delivery tool
sop: Assign the concept to the named squad in Jira Align.
Set the start date agreed with the squad lead.
Mirror the assignment on the PPM tool concept record.
Done when the assignment and start date exist in both tools.
verify: Open the concept record in both tools and compare the squad and dates.
Pass when both tools show the same squad and start date.

steps.title: Hand the squad lead the concept documentation
sop: Send the squad lead the concept brief, feasibility assessment, and business case.
Confirm the squad lead can access the source folders.
Record the handover in the concept record.
Done when the squad lead confirms receipt of all three documents.
verify: Check the handover record lists all three documents.
Pass when the squad lead has confirmed access to each.

steps.title: Schedule the kick-off with the concept owner invited
sop: Schedule the kick-off session for the assigned squad.
Include the concept owner on the invitation.
Circulate the agenda covering scope, milestones, and open questions.
Done when the kick-off is scheduled with the concept owner invited.
verify: Open the kick-off invitation and check the attendee list.
Pass when the concept owner is included and the date is set.

generic.Defined scope/population: The concept test of the leading proposition prototype with participants drawn from the target market segments.
generic.In-scope period: The testing window from prototype finalisation to capture of participant feedback.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each participant record carries segment, purchase intent score, willingness to pay, and objections captured.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Participant counts per segment reconcile to the recruitment quota and the CRM recruitment records.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Prototype version, test materials, and feedback dataset retained in SharePoint with test dates.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Segments under-recruited logged with the caveat applied to findings from that segment.
generic.Test population: Every concept test participant and every objection recorded during testing.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any test material reads as a binding quote or offer of insurance.
generic.Exception handling path: Materials that imply an offer are withdrawn and reissued with the concept disclaimer before further testing.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Testing is accepted when purchase intent and objection themes are documented with participant counts.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint concept test folder plus CRM participant records and the Excel feedback workbook.

steps.title: Build the prototype to represent the actual proposition
sop: Build the prototype including the intended price point and key exclusions.
Avoid presenting a proposition more attractive than the intended product.
Version the prototype and record what it represents.
Done when the prototype reflects price point and key exclusions.
verify: Compare the prototype against the concept requirements.
Pass when price point and key exclusions are both represented.

steps.title: Add the concept disclaimer to all test material
sop: Add wording stating the material is a concept and not an offer of insurance.
Place the disclaimer where participants will see it before responding.
Have the wording checked against the financial promotion standard.
Done when every test material carries the concept disclaimer.
verify: Review each test material for the disclaimer.
Pass when no material could be read as a binding quote or offer.

steps.title: Recruit participants from the documented target segments
sop: Select participants from the CRM matching the documented target segments.
Record the segment of each recruited participant.
Chase recruitment where a segment falls short of quota.
Done when participants cover the documented target segments.
verify: Compare recruited counts per segment against the quota.
Pass when every segment meets its quota or the shortfall is logged.

steps.title: Measure purchase intent and willingness to pay on a stated scale
sop: Use a defined numeric scale for purchase intent for every participant.
Capture willingness to pay against the presented price point.
Avoid recording impressions in place of scale responses.
Done when every participant has scale responses for both measures.
verify: Filter the feedback workbook for blank or non-scale responses.
Pass when every participant has scored responses on the stated scale.

steps.title: Capture objections and rejection reasons verbatim
sop: Record participant objections in their own words.
Capture the reason for rejection where a participant would not buy.
Group the verbatim objections into themes after collection.
Done when objections are captured verbatim and themed.
verify: Sample objection records for verbatim text.
Pass when objections are recorded verbatim rather than paraphrased only.

steps.title: Document purchase intent and objection themes with counts
sop: Summarise purchase intent distribution with participant counts.
Summarise objection themes with the count of participants raising each.
File the summary and dataset in the SharePoint concept test folder.
Done when intent and objection themes are documented with counts.
verify: Sum the theme counts against the participant total.
Pass when the counts reconcile to the participant population.

generic.Defined scope/population: The preliminary business case covering revenue projections, loss ratio assumptions, expenses, and time to market.
generic.In-scope period: At least three projection years from the assumed launch date plus the filing lead time window.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each assumption carries a value, source, owning function, and agreement record.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Revenue projections reconcile to the premium pool model produced at the opportunity stage.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Business case workbook versioned in SharePoint with the actuarial platform output references retained.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Assumptions no function will own logged as unowned with the escalation and resolution date.
generic.Test population: Every assumption row in the assumption register and every projection year in the model.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any loss ratio assumption has no cited basis or any material assumption has no owning function.
generic.Exception handling path: Unsupported loss ratio assumptions are replaced with an actuarial indication or flagged as provisional.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The case is accepted when the assumption register names an owning function for each assumption.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint business case workbook plus the actuarial modelling platform outputs and warehouse extracts.

steps.title: Project volume and average premium for three years
sop: Project policy volume separately for each of the first three years.
Project average premium separately for each year.
Derive revenue as the product of the two rather than as a single figure.
Done when volume and average premium are projected for three years.
verify: Inspect the projection tab for separate volume and premium rows per year.
Pass when three years each show volume and average premium separately.

steps.title: Set the loss ratio assumption from an evidenced basis
sop: Derive the loss ratio from a comparable book or an actuarial indication.
Run the supporting analysis on the actuarial modelling platform.
Cite the comparable or indication and its period in the assumption register.
Done when the loss ratio assumption cites an evidenced basis.
verify: Read the assumption register loss ratio row for its cited basis.
Pass when the basis is a comparable book or actuarial indication, not a target.

steps.title: Include expense and acquisition cost assumptions
sop: Add acquisition cost, servicing expense, and claims handling expense assumptions.
Source each from the warehouse expense data or Finance guidance.
Show expense assumptions separately from loss cost.
Done when expense and acquisition assumptions are present and sourced.
verify: Check the model for separate expense and acquisition lines.
Pass when expense assumptions are present and separately shown.

steps.title: Build the time-to-market estimate including filing lead times
sop: List the activities from approval to launch with their durations.
Add the filing submission and approval lead time per jurisdiction.
State the resulting launch date assumption in the model.
Done when the time-to-market estimate includes filing lead times.
verify: Compare the estimate against the jurisdiction filing lead times.
Pass when the estimate reflects the filing approval windows.

steps.title: Assign an owning function to each material assumption
sop: List every material assumption in the assumption register.
Name the function that owns and has agreed each assumption.
Obtain written agreement from each owning function.
Done when every material assumption has an agreeing owning function.
verify: Filter the assumption register for blank owning functions.
Pass when no material assumption is left unowned.

steps.title: Reconcile the case to the opportunity premium pool model
sop: Compare the business case premium projection against the premium pool model.
Explain any difference in scope, timing, or penetration assumption.
Adjust where the difference is an error rather than a scope change.
Done when the case reconciles to the premium pool model or the difference is explained.
verify: Read the reconciliation note against the two models.
Pass when the projections reconcile or the difference is documented.

generic.Defined scope/population: The reinsurance engagement covering treaty compatibility and facultative appetite for the product concept.
generic.In-scope period: The current treaty period and the renewal date constraining any required treaty amendment.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each reinsurer record carries approved counterparty status, response, appetite view, and indicative terms.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Reinsurers approached equal those on the approved counterparty list with no unapproved contacts.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Treaty wording check and reinsurer responses filed in SharePoint with the treaty version referenced.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Concepts requiring a treaty amendment logged with the renewal date constraint and the decision route.
generic.Test population: Every reinsurer approached and every treaty clause relevant to the concept.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any reinsurer approached is absent from the approved counterparty list.
generic.Exception handling path: Unapproved counterparty contact is escalated immediately and the engagement suspended pending approval.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Engagement is accepted when the concept coverage against current treaty terms is documented.
generic.Evidence location: Treaty repository wording check plus the reinsurance administration system engagement records.

steps.title: Check the concept against current treaty wording
sop: Retrieve the current treaty wording from the treaty repository.
Compare the concept coverage against the treaty scope and exclusions.
State whether the concept falls inside or outside existing cover.
Done when the treaty coverage position is documented.
verify: Read the coverage check against the treaty clauses cited.
Pass when the check names the treaty version and states the position.

steps.title: Confirm target reinsurers are on the approved counterparty list
sop: Retrieve the approved reinsurance counterparty list.
Check every reinsurer intended for approach against the list.
Remove any reinsurer not on the approved list from the approach plan.
Done when the approach list contains only approved counterparties.
verify: Match the approach list against the approved counterparty list.
Pass when every reinsurer on the approach list is approved.

steps.title: Approach reinsurers with the concept summary
sop: Send each approved reinsurer the concept summary and exposure profile.
Ask for a view on treaty compatibility and facultative appetite.
Record each approach in the reinsurance administration system.
Done when every approved reinsurer has been approached and logged.
verify: Check the reinsurance system for an engagement record per reinsurer.
Pass when every approach is logged with its date.

steps.title: Capture reinsurer responses in writing
sop: Collect each reinsurer response on compatibility and facultative appetite.
File the written response in the SharePoint reinsurance folder.
Chase reinsurers who have not responded by the deadline.
Done when every approached reinsurer has a written response or a logged non-response.
verify: Match responses against the approach list.
Pass when every approach has a written response or a logged non-response.

steps.title: Record indicative reinsurance cost or commission terms
sop: Extract indicative rate, commission, or ceding terms from each response.
Record them against the reinsurer in the engagement log.
Note where terms are indicative only and subject to full submission.
Done when indicative terms are recorded where offered.
verify: Read the engagement log terms column against the responses.
Pass when every offered term is captured with its indicative status.

steps.title: Flag concepts requiring a treaty amendment
sop: Identify where the concept would need a treaty amendment to be covered.
Record the treaty renewal date as the constraint on the amendment.
Escalate the timing constraint to the concept owner and the delivery schedule.
Done when amendment needs are flagged with their renewal date constraint.
verify: Read the flagged records for the renewal date constraint.
Pass when every amendment need cites the treaty renewal date.

generic.Defined scope/population: The design-thinking ideation sessions run with product and distribution teams on the validated customer problem.
generic.In-scope period: The ideation cycle from session scheduling to transfer of ideas into the backlog.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each idea carries a title, originator, session reference, and the phase in which it was raised.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Ideas transferred to the backlog equal the ideas captured in the session record.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Session record and idea list filed in Confluence and SharePoint with the session date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Ideas filtered out in the convergent phase retained with the reason they were not taken forward.
generic.Test population: Every idea raised across the ideation sessions in the cycle.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any idea is recorded without an originator or the session ideas are not transferred to the backlog.
generic.Exception handling path: Untransferred ideas are escalated to the session facilitator and loaded before the cycle closes.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Sessions are accepted when the full idea list is captured with an originator per idea.
generic.Evidence location: Confluence session page holding the idea list plus the SharePoint session record.

steps.title: Open each session with the validated problem statement
sop: Present the validated customer problem statement as the framing input.
Confirm participants understand the problem before ideation starts.
Record the problem statement version used in the session page.
Done when the session opens on the validated problem statement.
verify: Read the session page for the problem statement framing.
Pass when the session records the validated problem statement as the input.

steps.title: Confirm product and distribution participation
sop: Invite named product and distribution representatives to each session.
Chase any session with no distribution representative confirmed.
Record attendance from the Teams participant list.
Done when every session has product and distribution participation.
verify: Check the attendance record for both functions per session.
Pass when no session lacks a product or distribution participant.

steps.title: Run the divergent phase to generate ideas
sop: Run a divergent phase where ideas are generated without filtering.
Prevent evaluation or criticism during the divergent phase.
Capture every idea raised as it is spoken.
Done when the divergent phase closes with all ideas captured.
verify: Read the session page for a distinct divergent phase idea list.
Pass when ideas were generated before any filtering occurred.

steps.title: Record the originator against every idea
sop: Attribute each captured idea to the participant who raised it.
Include ideas that will not be taken forward with their originators.
Confirm attributions with participants before the session closes.
Done when every captured idea names its originator.
verify: Filter the idea list for blank originator values.
Pass when no idea is recorded without an originator.

steps.title: Run the convergent phase and record filtering reasons
sop: Run a convergent phase to shortlist ideas against the problem statement.
Record the reason each idea was or was not shortlisted.
Retain non-shortlisted ideas in the record rather than deleting them.
Done when the convergent phase closes with reasons recorded.
verify: Read the idea list for shortlist decisions and reasons.
Pass when every idea carries a shortlist decision with a reason.

steps.title: Transfer the session ideas into the idea backlog
sop: Load every captured idea into the idea backlog within the agreed timeframe.
Tag each backlog entry with the session reference and originator.
Publish the session record to Confluence and SharePoint.
Done when every session idea exists in the backlog with its session reference.
verify: Count backlog entries carrying the session reference against the session idea list.
Pass when the counts match with no idea left untransferred.

generic.Defined scope/population: The candidate product concepts documented from research inputs for the current screening cycle.
generic.In-scope period: The concept generation window between research synthesis and the concept scoring step.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each concept carries a unique concept ID, working name, customer problem, target segment, and coverage idea.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Concept count in the roadmap tool equals the concept count in the generation workbook.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Concept records versioned in SharePoint with the originating research artifact references.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Concepts duplicating in-force products logged with a differentiation note or removed.
generic.Test population: Every candidate concept recorded in the generation cycle.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any concept lacks a unique ID or an originating research reference.
generic.Exception handling path: Duplicate concepts are merged or given a documented differentiation note before scoring.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Concepts are accepted when each has a unique ID and an originating research reference.
generic.Evidence location: Product roadmap tool concept records plus the SharePoint concept generation workbook.

steps.title: Assemble the research inputs for concept generation
sop: Collect the validated needs, market scan, and ideation session outputs.
Record the artifact identifiers so concepts can cite them.
Confirm each input is the current version.
Done when the research input set is assembled with identifiers.
verify: Open each input from its recorded location.
Pass when every input resolves at the recorded version.

steps.title: Draft each concept with problem, segment, and coverage idea
sop: For each concept record the customer problem it addresses.
Record the target segment and the core coverage idea.
Write concepts at a consistent level of detail for comparability.
Done when every concept records problem, segment, and coverage idea.
verify: Filter concepts for blank problem, segment, or coverage fields.
Pass when no concept is missing any of the three.

steps.title: Cite the originating research finding for each concept
sop: Record the research finding or unmet need each concept originates from.
Cite the finding by identifier rather than by description.
Reject concepts with no traceable research origin.
Done when every concept cites an originating research finding.
verify: Filter concepts for blank research references.
Pass when no concept lacks an originating research citation.

steps.title: Assign a working name and unique concept ID
sop: Give each concept a short working name that distinguishes it.
Create the record in the roadmap tool so a unique concept ID is assigned.
Record the concept ID in the generation workbook.
Done when every concept has a working name and unique ID.
verify: Run a duplicate check on concept IDs and working names.
Pass when every concept ID is unique.

steps.title: Deduplicate against in-force products and in-flight initiatives
sop: Compare each concept against the in-force product catalogue.
Compare each concept against in-flight initiatives in the roadmap tool.
Merge duplicates or add a differentiation note where a concept is close.
Done when no concept duplicates an existing product without a note.
verify: Review flagged near-duplicates for a differentiation note.
Pass when no duplicate concept lacks a differentiation note.

steps.title: Publish the concept set for scoring
sop: Version the concept workbook and save it to the SharePoint cycle folder.
Confirm the roadmap tool concept records match the workbook.
Notify the scoring owner that the concept set is ready.
Done when the concept set is published and matches the tool records.
verify: Compare the workbook concept list against the roadmap tool records.
Pass when both hold the same concepts with matching IDs.

generic.Defined scope/population: The defined benchmark peer set assessed against every product concept on identical benchmark dimensions.
generic.In-scope period: The benchmark data vintage window with a retrieval date recorded per data point.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each benchmark cell carries a value, source, date, and the dimension it measures.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Benchmark dimension count applied to each concept is identical across all concepts scored.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Benchmarking workbook versioned in SharePoint with the warehouse extract date for internal comparators.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Dimensions with no obtainable peer data logged as gaps with the effect on the conclusion.
generic.Test population: Every benchmark data point across every peer and every concept.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any benchmark data point lacks a source and date or dimensions differ between concepts.
generic.Exception handling path: Unsourced data points are excluded from the scorecard inputs and logged as gaps.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Benchmarking is accepted when identical dimensions are applied to every concept with sourced data.
generic.Evidence location: The Excel benchmarking workbook plus the BI platform and warehouse extracts behind internal figures.

steps.title: Define the benchmark peer set with selection reasons
sop: Select the peer companies or products to benchmark against.
Record why each peer was chosen such as market overlap or product similarity.
Agree the peer set with the Insurance Product Manager before data collection.
Done when the peer set is defined with a documented reason per peer.
verify: Read the peer set table for selection reasons.
Pass when every peer has a recorded selection reason.

steps.title: Fix the benchmark dimensions applied to every concept
sop: Define the benchmark dimensions covering coverage, price, and distribution.
Lock the dimension list before scoring begins.
Apply the same dimensions to every concept without variation.
Done when the fixed dimension list is applied across all concepts.
verify: Compare the dimension columns across the concept tabs.
Pass when every concept is scored on identical dimensions.

steps.title: Collect peer coverage, price, and distribution data
sop: Gather peer data for each dimension from permitted sources.
Record the source name and retrieval date against each data point.
Log dimensions where no peer data can be obtained as gaps.
Done when every obtainable data point is collected and sourced.
verify: Filter the data grid for cells without a source or date.
Pass when no populated cell lacks a source and date.

steps.title: Load internal comparators from the warehouse
sop: Query the warehouse for our own position on each benchmark dimension.
Record the extract date and query on the source tab.
Cross-check the values against the BI platform reports.
Done when internal comparators are loaded and cross-checked.
verify: Compare the loaded internal values against the BI reports.
Pass when the two agree within the agreed tolerance.

steps.title: Call out white-space opportunities explicitly
sop: Identify dimensions where no peer competes meaningfully.
List each white-space opportunity explicitly rather than in narrative.
Note the evidence supporting each white-space claim.
Done when white-space opportunities are listed with evidence.
verify: Read the white-space list against the benchmark grid.
Pass when every white-space claim is supported by the grid data.

steps.title: Feed the benchmarking conclusions into the scorecard inputs
sop: Map each benchmark conclusion to the scorecard criterion it informs.
Transfer the values into the scorecard input tab.
Exclude gap-flagged dimensions from the scorecard inputs.
Done when scorecard inputs are populated from the benchmarking.
verify: Trace scorecard inputs back to the benchmarking grid.
Pass when every scorecard input maps to a sourced benchmark value.

generic.Defined scope/population: The shortlisted concepts presented to the Product Governance Committee at the stage-gate review.
generic.In-scope period: The committee cycle in which the concepts are tabled, bounded by the pre-read deadline.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Pack contains brief, scorecard, feasibility, and business case per concept with target market and outcome stated.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Concepts in the pack equal the shortlisted concept count in the pipeline register.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Pack lodged in the board portal with the issue timestamp and the minute filed in SharePoint.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Concepts deferred by the committee logged with the additional evidence required and the return date.
generic.Test population: Every concept in the stage-gate pack and every pack component per concept.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any concept is missing a pack component or the pack was issued after the pre-read deadline.
generic.Exception handling path: Incomplete concept packs are withdrawn from the agenda rather than presented partially.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The review is accepted when a decision is recorded for every concept presented.
generic.Evidence location: Board portal pack lodgement record plus the SharePoint committee minute and PPM register update.

steps.title: Assemble the pack components per shortlisted concept
sop: Collect the concept brief, scorecard, feasibility assessment, and preliminary business case.
Assemble one complete component set per shortlisted concept.
Flag any concept missing a component for completion or withdrawal.
Done when every concept has a complete component set.
verify: Check each concept section for all four components.
Pass when no concept in the pack is missing a component.

steps.title: State target market and expected customer outcome per concept
sop: For each concept state the intended target market explicitly.
State the customer outcome the product is expected to deliver.
Take both from the concept brief rather than restating them freshly.
Done when target market and customer outcome are stated per concept.
verify: Read each concept section for both statements.
Pass when no concept omits target market or customer outcome.

steps.title: Include concepts recommended for rejection in the pack
sop: Include concepts the team recommends rejecting alongside those to proceed.
State the recommendation and rationale for each concept.
Avoid filtering rejected recommendations out of the pack.
Done when both proceed and reject recommendations appear in the pack.
verify: Compare pack concepts against the full shortlist.
Pass when every shortlisted concept appears with a recommendation.

steps.title: Lodge the pack in the board portal before the pre-read deadline
sop: Upload the assembled pack to the board portal committee folder.
Confirm the lodgement timestamp precedes the pre-read deadline.
Notify committee members that the pack is available.
Done when the complete pack is lodged before the deadline.
verify: Compare the lodgement timestamp against the pre-read deadline.
Pass when lodgement precedes the deadline.

steps.title: Present the concepts at the Product Governance Committee
sop: Present each concept with its scorecard result and feasibility position.
Take committee questions and record them with the answers given.
Ask the committee to decide on each concept before moving on.
Done when every concept has been presented and decided.
verify: Check the session record for a decision against each concept.
Pass when no presented concept is left without a decision.

steps.title: Record the date, attendees, and decision per concept
sop: Record the presentation date and attendee list in the minute.
Record the decision and any conditions for each concept.
Circulate the minute for confirmation and file it in SharePoint.
Done when the minute records date, attendees, and per-concept decisions.
verify: Read the minute for the per-concept decision table.
Pass when every concept has a recorded decision in the minute.

generic.Defined scope/population: All concepts scored and ranked using the agreed weighted scorecard for the screening cycle.
generic.In-scope period: The scoring window after the weight set is agreed and before the stage-gate review.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Every concept has a score on every criterion with an evidence note per score.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Scorecard weights sum to the agreed total and the ranked list recalculates from the score matrix.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Scorecard workbook versioned in SharePoint with the weight agreement date recorded on the cover.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Concepts within a narrow score band flagged as effectively tied for committee judgement.
generic.Test population: Every score cell across every concept and criterion in the scorecard.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any score cell is blank or the weight agreement date does not precede the scoring date.
generic.Exception handling path: Blank scores are referred back to the scoring owner for completion before ranking is published.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Ranking is accepted when produced by the model formula rather than manual reordering.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint scorecard workbook holding the weight set, score matrix, and ranked output.

steps.title: Agree and record the scorecard weights before scoring
sop: Agree the weight for each scoring criterion with the governance forum.
Record the weight set and the agreement date on the workbook cover.
Lock the weight cells so they cannot change during scoring.
Done when the weight set is agreed, dated, and locked.
verify: Compare the weight agreement date against the scoring start date.
Pass when the agreement date precedes scoring.

steps.title: Load the concept set into the score matrix
sop: Load every concept from the generation workbook into the score matrix.
Carry across the concept ID and working name.
Confirm no concept is missing from the matrix.
Done when every concept appears in the score matrix.
verify: Compare matrix rows against the concept set count.
Pass when the counts match.

steps.title: Score every concept on every criterion
sop: Score each concept against each criterion using the defined scale.
Complete every cell so no criterion is skipped for any concept.
Escalate criteria that cannot be scored for lack of information.
Done when the score matrix has no blank cells.
verify: Filter the matrix for blank score cells.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Add an evidence note to each score
sop: For each score record a short note pointing to the supporting analysis.
Cite the feasibility, benchmarking, or business case artifact by name.
Avoid notes that restate the score without evidence.
Done when every score carries an evidence note.
verify: Filter score cells for missing evidence notes.
Pass when no score is left without an evidence note.

steps.title: Produce the ranked output from the model formula
sop: Calculate the weighted total for each concept using the workbook formula.
Sort the ranked output by the calculated total.
Avoid any manual reordering of the ranked list.
Done when the ranked list is produced by the formula.
verify: Recalculate the workbook and compare the order to the published ranking.
Pass when the published order matches the formula output.

steps.title: Flag concepts within a narrow score band as tied
sop: Identify concepts whose totals fall within the agreed tie threshold.
Flag them as effectively tied for committee judgement.
Note what would separate them if further evidence were obtained.
Done when concepts within the tie band are flagged.
verify: Compare adjacent score gaps against the tie threshold.
Pass when every pair inside the threshold is flagged as tied.

generic.Defined scope/population: All product concepts screened against strategic fit, regulatory feasibility, and actuarial viability criteria.
generic.In-scope period: The screening cycle bounded by the current strategy pillars and the regulatory position at the screening date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each concept carries a strategic, regulatory, and actuarial score plus the screening outcome and rationale.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Concepts passing screening equal the concept count that met every mandatory gate criterion.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Screening workbook versioned in SharePoint with GRC regulatory references and actuarial platform outputs cited.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Concepts failing a mandatory gate logged as screened out regardless of total score.
generic.Test population: Every concept in the screening cycle across all three scoring dimensions.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any concept lacks one of the three scores or passes despite failing a mandatory gate criterion.
generic.Exception handling path: Concepts failing a mandatory gate are moved to screened out and archived with the rationale.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Screening is accepted when strategic, regulatory, and actuarial scores exist for every concept.
generic.Evidence location: The Excel screening workbook plus GRC platform filing references and actuarial platform outputs.

steps.title: Score strategic fit against the claimed pillar
sop: Identify the strategic pillar each concept claims to serve.
Score strategic fit against that named pillar, not the strategy generally.
Record the pillar reference alongside the score.
Done when every concept has a strategic fit score against a named pillar.
verify: Filter concepts for blank strategic scores or pillar references.
Pass when no concept is missing either.

steps.title: Score regulatory feasibility from the GRC filing position
sop: Pull the filing and licensing position per target jurisdiction from the GRC platform.
Score regulatory feasibility using that position rather than assumption.
Cite the GRC record reference alongside the score.
Done when every concept has a regulatory score citing the GRC position.
verify: Trace a sample of regulatory scores to their GRC references.
Pass when each sampled score cites a GRC record.

steps.title: Score actuarial viability from the actuarial view
sop: Assess data availability and loss predictability for each concept.
Run supporting analysis on the actuarial modelling platform where needed.
Provide a viability score with the reasoning recorded.
Done when every concept has an actuarial viability score.
verify: Filter concepts for blank actuarial scores.
Pass when no concept is missing an actuarial score.

steps.title: Apply the mandatory gate criteria
sop: Identify the mandatory gate criteria that cannot be traded off.
Mark any concept failing a mandatory gate as screened out.
Apply this regardless of the concept total score.
Done when every mandatory gate failure is marked screened out.
verify: Cross-check passing concepts against the mandatory gate results.
Pass when no concept passes screening despite a mandatory gate failure.

steps.title: Write the screening outcome and rationale per concept
sop: Record the screening outcome as pass or screened out for each concept.
Write the rationale naming the decisive criterion.
Attach the rationale to the concept record.
Done when every concept carries an outcome and a rationale.
verify: Filter concepts for blank outcomes or rationales.
Pass when no concept is missing either.

steps.title: Version and file the screening workbook
sop: Version the workbook and stamp the screening date.
File it in the SharePoint screening cycle folder.
Notify the governance committee secretary that screening is complete.
Done when the versioned screening workbook is filed.
verify: Open the filed workbook and check the three score columns.
Pass when all three scores are present for every concept.

generic.Defined scope/population: The milestone schedule for the concept's next development stage including filings, pricing, configuration, and readiness.
generic.In-scope period: The next development stage from kick-off to the following stage-gate review date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each milestone carries a name, target date, accountable owner, and dependency links where relevant.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Milestones in the roadmap tool match the baselined schedule in the PPM tool with no divergence.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Baselined schedule retained in the PPM tool with the baseline date recorded.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Milestones without a confirmed owner logged with the escalation and the resolution date.
generic.Test population: Every milestone in the next-stage schedule for the concept.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any milestone has no accountable owner or the schedule is not baselined.
generic.Exception handling path: Unowned milestones are escalated to the delivery lead before the schedule is baselined.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The schedule is accepted when baselined with an owner and date on every milestone.
generic.Evidence location: PPM tool baselined schedule plus the product roadmap tool milestone view.

steps.title: List the next-stage milestones for the concept
sop: List the milestones required to complete the next development stage.
Include design, pricing, configuration, and readiness milestones.
Record each milestone with a clear completion definition.
Done when the milestone list covers the next stage.
verify: Compare the milestone list against the stage definition.
Pass when every required stage activity has a milestone.

steps.title: Add regulatory filing submission and approval milestones
sop: Add a filing submission milestone per target jurisdiction.
Add the corresponding approval milestone using the jurisdiction lead time.
Check the lead times against the constraint analysis.
Done when filing submission and approval milestones exist per jurisdiction.
verify: Compare the filing milestone gaps against the recorded lead times.
Pass when each gap reflects the jurisdiction approval lead time.

steps.title: Add dependency milestones for pricing, configuration, and distribution
sop: Add milestones for actuarial pricing completion and system configuration.
Add a distribution readiness milestone for channel enablement.
Link dependent milestones with predecessor relationships.
Done when the three dependency milestones exist and are linked.
verify: Open the dependency view in the PPM tool.
Pass when pricing, configuration, and distribution milestones are present and linked.

steps.title: Assign an accountable owner to every milestone
sop: Name the accountable owner for each milestone.
Confirm each owner accepts the milestone and its date.
Escalate milestones where no owner will accept.
Done when every milestone has an accepting accountable owner.
verify: Filter the schedule for milestones with blank owners.
Pass when no milestone is left without an owner.

steps.title: Set the next stage-gate review date in the schedule
sop: Identify the committee cycle for the next stage gate.
Set the gate review date as a milestone in the schedule.
Work back to confirm preceding milestones complete before the gate.
Done when the next gate review date is in the schedule.
verify: Check the gate milestone date against the committee calendar.
Pass when the gate date aligns to a scheduled committee cycle.

steps.title: Baseline the schedule in the PPM tool
sop: Baseline the milestone schedule so later slippage can be measured.
Record the baseline date and version.
Mirror the milestone dates into the roadmap tool.
Done when the schedule is baselined and mirrored.
verify: Compare the PPM baseline against the roadmap tool milestone dates.
Pass when both tools show the same baselined dates.

generic.Defined scope/population: All concepts approved at the stage gate and their entries in the product pipeline register.
generic.In-scope period: The stage-gate cycle in which the approvals were minuted.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each approved concept carries approved status, minute reference, decision date, owner, squad, and next milestone.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Approved concept count in the register equals the approved count in the committee minute.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Register update retained in the PPM tool with the update timestamp and minute reference.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Conditions attached to any approval recorded on the register entry with owners and due dates.
generic.Test population: Every concept marked approved in the register for the cycle.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any concept is marked approved without a committee decision reference.
generic.Exception handling path: Concepts approved in the register without a minute reference are reverted pending confirmation.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The update is accepted when approved status and minute reference exist on every approved concept.
generic.Evidence location: PPM tool pipeline register entries plus the Excel reconciliation against the committee minute.

steps.title: Extract the approved concept list from the committee minute
sop: Read the committee minute and list every concept approved.
Record the decision date and the minute reference for each.
Note conditions attached to any approval.
Done when the approved list with references is extracted.
verify: Compare the extracted list against the minute decision table.
Pass when every minuted approval appears in the list.

steps.title: Set approved status on each register entry
sop: Open each approved concept in the PPM pipeline register.
Set the status to approved and record the decision date.
Enter the committee minute reference against the entry.
Done when every approved concept shows approved status with a minute reference.
verify: Run the register report for approved concepts without a minute reference.
Pass when the report returns no rows.

steps.title: Record owner, squad, and next milestone date
sop: Record the assigned owner and development squad on each approved concept.
Record the next milestone date from the baselined schedule.
Correct entries where the squad assignment is not yet made.
Done when owner, squad, and next milestone are recorded.
verify: Filter approved concepts for blank owner, squad, or milestone date.
Pass when no approved concept is missing any of the three.

steps.title: Record approval conditions on the register entries
sop: Enter each condition from the minute against the relevant concept.
Assign the condition owner and the gate it must be met by.
Set the condition to open so it is tracked to closure.
Done when every minuted condition is recorded and open.
verify: Count register conditions against the conditions in the minute.
Pass when the counts match with none omitted.

steps.title: Reconcile the register count to the minute count
sop: Export the approved concept list from the register into Excel.
Compare the count and the concept identifiers against the minute.
Investigate and correct any difference.
Done when the register approved count reconciles to the minute.
verify: Read the reconciliation difference figure.
Pass when the difference is zero.

steps.title: Review the updated register entries
sop: Review each updated entry against the minute wording.
Confirm no concept was marked approved that the committee deferred.
Sign off the register update with a date.
Done when the review is signed and no discrepancy remains.
verify: Compare register statuses against the minute decisions.
Pass when every status matches the minuted decision.

generic.Defined scope/population: The investment business case covering market size, premium projections, loss ratio, expense assumptions, and customer outcome.
generic.In-scope period: The projection horizon of the business case from investment start through the payback window.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each assumption carries owner, source, value, and sensitivity, and each section is separately documented.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Premium projections reconcile to the opportunity-stage sizing model with variances explained.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Business case workbook and document versioned in SharePoint with the warehouse extract date recorded.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Assumptions with no agreed owner logged as unowned with the escalation and resolution date.
generic.Test population: Every assumption row and every projection section in the business case.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any assumption lacks an owner and source or the premium projection contradicts the sizing model.
generic.Exception handling path: Inconsistent projections are reconciled or the difference documented before the case goes to committee.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The case is accepted when the assumption register lists owner and source for every assumption.
generic.Evidence location: SharePoint business case folder plus the warehouse extracts behind the market and premium figures.

steps.title: Document market size as a separate case section
sop: Carry the market sizing result into a dedicated business case section.
Cite the sizing model version and its extract date.
State the TAM, SAM, and SOM separately as in the source model.
Done when the market size section is documented with citations.
verify: Compare the section figures against the sizing model.
Pass when the figures match the cited sizing model version.

steps.title: Build the premium projection section
sop: Project premium by year using volume and average premium drivers.
Query the warehouse for comparable book data to anchor the drivers.
Record the extract date for the warehouse inputs.
Done when the premium projection is built with dated inputs.
verify: Reconcile the projection against the sizing model penetration assumption.
Pass when the projection is consistent with the sizing model.

steps.title: Document the loss ratio assumption section
sop: State the loss ratio assumption and the basis it rests on.
Cite the comparable book or actuarial indication used.
Record the sensitivity of the case to the loss ratio.
Done when the loss ratio section states basis and sensitivity.
verify: Read the loss ratio section for its cited basis.
Pass when the basis is evidenced rather than a target.

steps.title: Document expense assumptions across all cost types
sop: Include acquisition, servicing, claims handling, and filing cost assumptions.
Source each from Finance guidance or warehouse expense data.
Show each cost type separately in the expense section.
Done when all four expense types are documented and sourced.
verify: Check the expense section for the four cost types.
Pass when each type is present with a source.

steps.title: State the customer outcome the product delivers
sop: Describe the customer outcome and value the product delivers.
Link the outcome to the validated customer needs from research.
Place it in the case alongside the financial sections.
Done when the customer outcome section is written and linked to research.
verify: Read the customer outcome section for its research link.
Pass when the outcome cites a validated customer need.

steps.title: Complete the assumption register with owner and sensitivity
sop: List every assumption used across the case sections.
Record owner, source, value, and sensitivity for each.
Obtain owner agreement for each material assumption.
Done when the assumption register is complete for every assumption.
verify: Filter the register for blank owner or source cells.
Pass when no assumption is missing an owner or a source.

steps.title: Version and file the assembled business case
sop: Assemble the sections into the business case document.
Version the document and workbook consistently.
File both in the SharePoint business case folder.
Done when the versioned case and workbook are filed together.
verify: Open the filed case and check the version matches the workbook.
Pass when document and workbook versions align.

generic.Defined scope/population: The ROI, NPV, and payback calculation for the initiative measured against the internal hurdle rate.
generic.In-scope period: The full cash flow horizon from investment start through payback and the case projection end.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Discount rate, hurdle rate, ROI, NPV, payback in months, and the pass or fail conclusion are populated.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: The cash flow profile totals reconcile to the investment estimate and premium projection in the business case.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Calculation workbook versioned with the Finance-published rate source and its publication date cited.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Deviations from the published hurdle rate logged with the Finance approval for the deviation.
generic.Test population: Every rate input and every calculated measure in the ROI workbook.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if the hurdle or discount rate is hardcoded and differs from the current Finance policy rate.
generic.Exception handling path: Rate mismatches are corrected to the Finance-published rate and the calculation rerun.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The calculation is accepted when ROI, NPV, and payback are all shown with the hurdle rate source cited.
generic.Evidence location: The Excel calculation workbook plus the ERP general ledger source for the Finance-published rates.

steps.title: Retrieve the current Finance discount and hurdle rates
sop: Obtain the current published discount and hurdle rates from Finance.
Record the publication reference and date on the workbook source tab.
Link the rate cells to the source tab rather than typing values.
Done when both rates are loaded from the Finance-published source.
verify: Trace the rate cells back to the source tab.
Pass when both rates reference the Finance-published figures.

steps.title: Build the cash flow profile including the full outlay
sop: Enter the investment outlay by period from the investment estimate.
Enter the premium and expense flows by period from the business case.
Ensure outlay appears before any earned premium in the profile.
Done when the cash flow profile spans outlay through the projection end.
verify: Sum the outlay in the profile against the investment estimate total.
Pass when the two totals reconcile.

steps.title: Reconcile the profile to the ERP cost lines
sop: Compare the investment cost lines against the ERP budget lines for the initiative.
Confirm the cost categories match the ledger structure.
Resolve any difference with the Finance business partner.
Done when the profile reconciles to the ERP cost lines.
verify: Read the reconciliation note against the ERP extract.
Pass when the differences are zero or explained.

steps.title: Calculate ROI, NPV, and payback period
sop: Calculate NPV using the Finance discount rate from the source tab.
Calculate ROI over the projection horizon.
Calculate payback in months from launch and from investment start.
Done when all three measures are calculated and displayed.
verify: Check all three measures appear on the output tab.
Pass when ROI, NPV, and payback are each shown.

steps.title: Compare the result against the hurdle rate
sop: Compare the calculated return against the hurdle rate.
State a clear pass or fail conclusion on the output tab.
Note the margin by which the hurdle is met or missed.
Done when a pass or fail conclusion is stated with its margin.
verify: Read the output tab conclusion.
Pass when an explicit pass or fail conclusion is stated.

steps.title: Audit the workbook for hardcoded rate values
sop: Run a formula audit for hardcoded rates in calculation cells.
Replace any hardcoded rate with a reference to the source tab.
Recalculate and confirm the results are unchanged or corrected.
Done when no calculation cell holds a hardcoded rate.
verify: Compare every rate used against the Finance-published figures.
Pass when no rate in the workbook differs from the current policy rate.

generic.Defined scope/population: The funding approval notification issued to the named product owner and their line manager.
generic.In-scope period: The notification window from the recorded funding decision to filing of the notification evidence.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Notification states funding amount, conditions in full, effective date, and the minute or decision reference.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: The funding figure in the notification equals the amount recorded in the approval decision.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Sent notification filed against the initiative record in the PPM tool with its send timestamp.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Delivery failures logged with the resend action and the confirmed delivery date.
generic.Test population: The notification content and the recipient list against the approval decision record.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if the notification funding figure differs from the recorded decision or a condition is summarised.
generic.Exception handling path: Any figure or condition discrepancy triggers a corrected notification before filing.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The notification is accepted when filed with funding amount and conditions stated in full.
generic.Evidence location: PPM tool initiative record attachment plus the sent item in Microsoft Teams or Email.

steps.title: Retrieve the recorded funding decision
sop: Open the approval decision record in the PPM tool.
Record the approved amount, phasing, conditions, and effective date.
Note the committee minute or decision reference.
Done when the decision details are captured from the record.
verify: Compare the captured details against the committee minute.
